result: After validation on Hamiltonians with known transitions, the agent recovered Neel, Haldane, and dimerized phases of a frustrated bilinear-biquadratic spin-1 chain with single-ion anisotropy, plus incommensurate correlations and frustration-dependent boundary geometry, within an eight-hour compute budget.
conclusion: The work suggests a practical route to autonomous computational discovery of quantum phases of matter, though it is an AI-for-physics tool rather than a result in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Beam Search For Error-Correcting Codes Via Conditional Diffusion
authors: Henry D. Pfister Ziv Aharoni
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a diffusion framework for neural decoding of error-correcting codes (ECCs). We interpret decoding as a conditional diffusion process that progressively predicts codeword bits while treating the physical channel observation as fixed side information. At each stage, a neural model estimates bitwise posteriors conditioned on the physical observation and the current noisy state of the codeword. We focus particularly on masked diffusion, for which the reverse process naturally induces a Maxwell beam search (MBS) procedure inspired by the Maxwell construction of Measson et al. Rather than committing to a single uncertain decision, the decoder maintains multiple candidate trajectories, removes parity-infeasible candidates, and ranks the remaining candidates using accumulated reverse-transition log-probabilities. We evaluate the framework across multiple code families on binary phase-shift keying (BPSK) over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). Experiments show competitive decoding performance across Polar, low-density parity-check (LDPC), and Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes. The MBS decoder consistently improves upon the corresponding single-trajectory diffusion decoder and, in all evaluated settings, improves upon available neural decoding results.
tldr: A conditional diffusion framework with a Maxwell beam search decoder is proposed for neural decoding of classical error-correcting codes (Polar, LDPC, BCH) over BPSK/AWGN channels.
motivation: Neural decoders for error-correcting codes typically commit to hard decisions along a single trajectory, which is fragile near code boundaries; the authors aim to exploit the structure of diffusion reverse processes to retain and rank multiple candidate codewords.
method: Decoding is cast as a masked conditional diffusion process in which a neural network estimates bitwise posteriors given the channel observation, and the reverse process induces a 'Maxwell beam search' that keeps multiple trajectories, prunes parity-infeasible candidates, and ranks survivors by accumulated reverse-transition log-probabilities.
result: Experiments on BPSK/AWGN across Polar, LDPC, and BCH code families show that the Maxwell beam search decoder consistently outperforms the single-trajectory diffusion decoder and improves on previously reported neural decoding results in all evaluated settings.
conclusion: Combining conditional diffusion with beam-search-style candidate management yields a competitive, code-agnostic neural decoding scheme for classical channel coding.

title: Settling Nondeterministic Communication Complexity Of Graph Connectivity
authors: Zhijun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining the communication complexity of graph connectivity has been one of the longest standing open problems in communication complexity since the seminal work of Babai, Frankl, and Simon [FOCS'86]. A simple protocol transmits a spanning forest using [MATH] communication on [MATH]-vertex graphs. While this was shown optimal for deterministic protocols by Hajnal, Maass, and Tur\'an [STOC'88], the optimal nondeterministic and randomized complexities have remained unresolved for decades. We settle the nondeterministic communication complexity of graph connectivity by proving an optimal [MATH] lower bound. The best prior bound was [MATH] due to Raz and Spieker [Combinatorica'95]. Our bound is shown by upper bounding the maximum size of [MATH]-monochromatic rectangles. Generalizing our techniques to weighted, almost [MATH]-monochromatic rectangles yields an [MATH] lower bound for randomized protocols with error probability [MATH]. In particular, this bound is optimal for any polynomially small [MATH]. For constant error probability, we also prove that any [MATH]-round protocol requires [MATH] communication, which is optimal for every constant [MATH]. Previously, optimal [MATH] lower bounds for graph connectivity were known only for [MATH]-round [Sun, Woodruff; APPROX/RANDOM'15] and [MATH]-round protocols [Radhakrishnan, Reddy, Venkat; ITCS'26]. Our proof introduces a new communication problem which can be viewed as a composition of inner product and pointer chasing problems. Our lower bounds can be extended to other fundamental graph properties, and also imply optimality of known query and streaming algorithms for related problems.
tldr: The paper settles the long-open nondeterministic communication complexity of graph connectivity by proving an optimal Ω(n log n)-type lower bound via a bound on monochromatic rectangle sizes, with extensions to randomized and round-restricted protocols.
motivation: The communication complexity of graph connectivity has been open since Babai–Frankl–Simon (1986); the deterministic bound was settled in 1988, but optimal nondeterministic and randomized complexities remained unresolved for decades, with the best prior nondeterministic lower bound due to Raz and Spieker.
method: The author upper bounds the maximum size of monochromatic rectangles for the connectivity problem, introducing a new communication problem seen as a composition of inner product and pointer chasing, and generalizes the argument to almost-monochromatic rectangles to handle bounded-error randomized protocols and round-restricted protocols.
result: An optimal nondeterministic lower bound matching the spanning-forest upper bound is proven, along with an Ω(n log n / log log n)-type randomized lower bound optimal for polynomially small error, and an optimal round-by-round tradeoff for constant error; the techniques extend to other graph properties and yield optimality of known query and streaming algorithms.
conclusion: The work closes a decades-old open problem in classical communication complexity and provides a versatile lower-bound framework, but it contains no quantum information, thermodynamic, networking, or hybrid-platform content.

title: Thermal-noise-limited Stabilization Of A Self-injection-locked Diode Laser Using A Miniature Fabry-Perot Cavity
authors: Alexander K. Vorobyev, Olga V. Khronusova, Nikita O. Zhadnov, Konstantin S. Kudeyarov, Denis S. Kryuchkov, Danila V. Morozov, Nikita Yu. Dmitriev, Artem E. Shitikov, Dmitry A. Chermoshentsev, Igor A. Bilenko, Nikolai N. Kolachevsky
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an ultrastable laser system based on miniature core components: a self-injection-locked laser comprising a distributed-feedback laser diode and an integrated microring resonator, together with a 3-ml vacuum-gap Fabry-Perot cavity. By carefully addressing technical noise sources, in particular residual amplitude modulation, we demonstrate a thermal-noise-limited fractional frequency instability of [MATH] for averaging times between 1 and 10 s, which is among the lowest reported for compact cavity-stabilized lasers. This performance is achieved with conventional multilayer mirrors and a moderate cavity finesse of [MATH]. Such stability of the output frequency, combined with the small size of the core components and a possibility to generate a Kerr frequency comb in the very same microring resonator, provides a path towards fully integrated photonic frequency references for transportable optical clocks and low-noise microwave synthesis.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a compact ultrastable laser stabilized to a miniature Fabry-Perot cavity, achieving thermal-noise-limited frequency instability suitable for transportable optical clocks and low-noise microwave synthesis.
motivation: Compact and robust ultrastable lasers are needed for field-deployable optical clocks and integrated photonic frequency references, but technical noise and thermal noise limit miniaturized cavity-stabilized systems.
method: The authors combine a self-injection-locked distributed-feedback diode laser with an integrated microring resonator and a 3-ml vacuum-gap Fabry-Perot cavity, carefully suppressing technical noise such as residual amplitude modulation.
result: They achieve a thermal-noise-limited fractional frequency instability in the low 10^-15 range for averaging times between 1 and 10 s, among the best reported for compact cavity-stabilized lasers using conventional multilayer mirrors and moderate finesse.
conclusion: The compact laser system provides a path toward fully integrated photonic frequency references for transportable optical clocks and low-noise microwave generation.

title: Photoelectrons Resolve The Phase-dependent Variance Of Bright Squeezed Vacuum
authors: Haoran Ma, Yihe Wang, Chuan Cheng, Ian Gabalski, Aaron M. Ghrist, Eleanor Weckwerth, Mohammed Th. Hassan, Philip H. Bucksbaum
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The variance of bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) is not only strong but also phase dependent, yet recent strong-field experiments with BSV have recorded only its magnitude. A coherent field of the same color provides the phase reference that resolves this phase-dependent noise. Strong-field ionization of xenon by this light shows that the photoelectron yield follows the BSV quadrature along the coherent field, and that the nonlinearity of ionization amplifies the quadrature noise many times over in the electron yield. The noise is moreover distributed unevenly over the photoelectron momentum distribution, differing by an order of magnitude between ionization channels. Strong-field ionization thus offers a phase-sensitive, channel-resolved detector of quantum light, while the quadrature noise of quantum light offers a probe of the intensity dependence of individual ionization pathways.
tldr: The paper shows that strong-field ionization of xenon by bright squeezed vacuum mixed with a coherent reference resolves the phase-dependent quadrature noise of quantum light in the photoelectron yield.
motivation: Bright squeezed vacuum has phase-dependent variance, but previous strong-field experiments measured only its magnitude. A phase reference is needed to access the quadrature-resolved noise in ionization experiments.
method: The authors combine bright squeezed vacuum with a coherent field of the same color and use strong-field ionization of xenon as a phase-sensitive, channel-resolved detector, comparing photoelectron yields to the BSV quadrature along the coherent field.
result: Photoelectron yield follows the BSV quadrature, with ionization nonlinearity amplifying quadrature noise in the electron yield; the noise varies by up to an order of magnitude across ionization channels and is unevenly distributed in momentum.
conclusion: Strong-field ionization provides a phase-sensitive detector of quantum light, while quadrature noise can probe intensity dependence of individual ionization pathways.

title: Conviction Versus Conformity In A Random-Field Ising Electorate: Antagonistic Ties, Network Density, And A Parameter-Free Prediction
authors: Natalia Romero
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the zero-temperature random-field Ising model with +-J bond disorder on sparse graphs as a model of an electorate: survey-derived, trimodal fields compete with social couplings, a fraction alpha of which are antagonistic. With exact ground states up to N=180 (over 78000 optimizations, certified except in the densest frustrated cases) and validated heuristics to N=720, we locate the crossover r_h* at which the field carries half of the ground-state energy, close to where half the voters held against their own field have switched (0.93 r_h* for alpha<=0.2). Our main test is a zero-temperature cavity theory solved on the graph ensemble with no fitted parameter: at seven densities not otherwise used, predicted before their exact ground states were computed, it placed r_h* within 10% in 19 of 21 cells (median error 3%). Its errors are unsigned at alpha=0.05 and 0.5 but all negative at alpha=0.2, where it predicts the coupling energy correctly but a crossover that is early and, at high density, too sharp, and where its replica-symmetric solution is unstable in six of seven cells, consistent with replica-symmetry breaking at intermediate frustration. Empirically r_h*~0.91 e_J(0), with e_J(0) the coupling energy of the zero-field ground state, inside a rigorous per-instance factor-of-two window, so the known +-J energy laws carry over: r_h* ~ ^gamma with gamma=1.01-1.09 for alpha=0.05 and 0.50-0.57 for alpha>=0.5 (=3-28; five graph families agree at matched density). At intermediate frustration r_h* is not a power law: sparse networks accommodate antagonistic ties at the cost of cooperative ones, which stops paying near ~10; the theory reproduces this without adjustment. In weakly frustrated dense networks the ground state is a near-consensus following the sign of the aggregate field in 93-100% of realisations at small r_h, against near-chance agreement in frustrated ones.
tldr: The paper analyzes a zero-temperature random-field Ising model with random-sign (antagonistic) couplings on sparse graphs as a stylized model of an electorate, testing a parameter-free cavity-theory prediction of the field-energy crossover against exact ground states.
motivation: The authors aim to model opinion formation in a population where survey-derived fields compete with social interactions, some of which are antagonistic, and to test whether an analytically derived cavity theory can predict the behavior without any fitting.
method: Exact ground-state optimization for systems up to N=180 across more than 78000 instances (with validated heuristics up to N=720), combined with a zero-temperature replica-symmetric cavity theory solved on the graph ensemble and compared against predictions made before exact computation at seven previously unused densities.
result: The cavity prediction located the crossover r_h* within 10% in 19 of 21 cells (median error 3%), with systematic negative errors at intermediate frustration alpha=0.2 where the replica-symmetric solution is unstable in six of seven cells; scaling r_h* ~ r^gamma with gamma ~ 1.01-1.09 and 0.50-0.57 for the two alpha regimes is observed.
conclusion: Random-field Ising spin-glass techniques with +-J disorder describe electorate-like models quantitatively even at intermediate frustration, with replica-symmetry breaking plausibly responsible for the residual discrepancies at high density.

title: Photon-Number Discrimination From Increasing Time-of-Arrival Separation In Wide Superconducting Microstrip Single-Photon Detectors
authors: Hsin-Yeh Wu, Shu-Xiao Liu, Boris Tuchming, Xavier-Fran\c{c}ois Navick, Pu-Kai Wang, Yi-Ren Wu, Jia-Wern Chen, Marc Besan\c{c}on, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Glicenstein, Pisin Chen, Yu-Jung Lu, Stathes Paganis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Measurements of photon-number-dependent time-of-arrival (TOA) distributions in wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors (SMSPDs) are presented. Two {\um}-long devices with widths of {\um} and {\um} are characterized under pulsed {nm} excitation. The TOA histograms are described by sums of exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) components, with the wider device exhibiting components assigned to photon numbers up to \(n=8\). Adjacent TOA peaks become more distinguishable relative to their widths at higher photon number, in contrast to the compression of neighboring photon-number timing shifts observed in conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs. For the components assigned to \(n=7\) and \(n=8\), the FWHM-normalized peak separation is \(2.15\), and the fitted EMG distributions yield an equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity of \(99.6\%\). The EMG exponential-tail parameter \(\tau_n\) decreases strongly with photon number, while the Gaussian-location parameter \(\mu_n\) continues to shift between neighboring components. A phenomenological model motivated by absorption-site-dependent vortex processes and collective current redistribution captures these timing trends. These results support wide SMSPDs as a platform for TOA-based photon-number discrimination at high photon number, relevant to multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing. The same geometry also provides a setting to examine how the spatial distribution of photon absorption affects vortex-assisted detection.
tldr: The paper characterizes wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors and shows improved time-of-arrival separation for photon-number discrimination up to n=8.
motivation: Photon-number-resolved detection is useful for multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing, but conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs suffer from compressed timing shifts between adjacent photon numbers.
method: Two-micrometer-long wide SMSPDs are measured under pulsed excitation, and their time-of-arrival histograms are fitted with sums of exponentially modified Gaussian components assigned to different photon numbers.
result: The wider device resolves components up to n=8, with FWHM-normalized peak separation 2.15 and 99.6% equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity for n=7 and n=8; a phenomenological vortex/current-redistribution model captures the timing trends.
conclusion: Wide SMSPDs are promising for TOA-based high-photon-number discrimination, but the work is primarily detector characterization rather than a core contribution to the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems directions.

title: Bogoliubov Dynamics And Zitterbewegung In Optical Dirac Systems
authors: Lili Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a bosonic Bogoliubov description of Zitterbewegung in time-dependent optical-Dirac systems. Within the optical-Dirac framework, the anomalous pair-creation and pair-annihilation terms of a bosonic Bogoliubov Hamiltonian correspond to couplings between the positive- and negative-frequency sectors, whose coherence underlies the Zitterbewegung response. When the constitutive parameters vary in time, the resulting moving-frame connection generates dynamical interbranch coupling and positive--negative-frequency coherence. Under periodic modulation, this coupling becomes resonant near [MATH], leading to parametric amplification of the coherence and consequently to an enhanced Zitterbewegung motion.
tldr: The paper develops a bosonic Bogoliubov framework for Zitterbewegung in time-dependent optical-Dirac systems, showing that periodic modulation can resonantly amplify positive-negative-frequency coherence.
motivation: Zitterbewegung and interbranch coherence in optical-Dirac systems are typically studied in static or slowly varying settings; the authors aim to understand how time-dependent constitutive parameters dynamically generate and enhance such effects.
method: They formulate a bosonic Bogoliubov Hamiltonian for optical-Dirac systems, identify anomalous pair-creation/annihilation terms as positive-negative-frequency couplings, and analyze the moving-frame connection induced by time-varying parameters, including periodic modulation.
result: Periodic modulation produces resonant dynamical interbranch coupling near a specific condition, leading to parametric amplification of positive-negative-frequency coherence and enhanced Zitterbewegung motion.
conclusion: Time-dependent Bogoliubov dynamics provides a route to control and amplify Zitterbewegung in optical-Dirac platforms via resonant parametric modulation.

title: High Resolution Hyperspectral Quantum Infrared Imaging With Undetected Photons
authors: Aadi Suketu Bharatia, Vidya Prakash Muppalla, Ananya Asthana, Priyanka Kandankel, Tanmoy Chakraborty, Sreelaja Nair, Anshuman Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum sensing in the infrared regime often demands the use of expensive and cryogenically operated detectors. Nonlinear interferometry has paved the way for information transfer from the infrared to the near--infrared or visible regime in various quantum technologies. A particularly interesting application of these interferometers involves spectrally--resolved quantum imaging using undetected photons, enabled by the use of temperature--tunable parametric amplifiers. In this work, we demonstrate spectrally resolved transmission imaging with undetected photons around 1550 nm using a spontaneous parametric down conversion based folded nonlinear interferometric scheme, registering the attenuation of a zebrafish larva as a biological feasibility test. We characterize and calibrate the interferometer, having achieved spectrally resolved interference fringes with a maximum baseline visibility of [MATH] in the near--infrared regime. Phase--stepped readout of a grating spectrometer gives a resolving power of [MATH] (from the spectrometer's point spread function) at 1550 nm, and [MATH] from the coherence length, the finest reported for imaging with undetected photons, over an instantaneous spectral window of [MATH] cm[MATH].
tldr: The paper demonstrates high-resolution hyperspectral infrared imaging with undetected photons using a folded nonlinear interferometer and SPDC, with a biological feasibility test on a zebrafish larva.
motivation: Infrared quantum sensing typically requires expensive cryogenic detectors, so nonlinear interferometry can transfer information from infrared to near-infrared/visible regimes for spectrally resolved imaging.
method: A spontaneous parametric down-conversion based folded nonlinear interferometric scheme with temperature-tunable parametric amplifiers is characterized and calibrated for spectrally resolved transmission imaging around 1550 nm.
result: The authors achieve spectrally resolved interference fringes with high baseline visibility and report a resolving power of up to about 10^4 at 1550 nm over an instantaneous spectral window, demonstrating imaging of a zebrafish larva.
conclusion: The work establishes a practical hyperspectral quantum infrared imaging technique with undetected photons, offering fine spectral resolution and biological applicability.

title: Banded Chaos And Time-Semicrystalline Order
authors: Matteo Baggioli
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work has introduced the notion of a time semicrystal, a driven nonequilibrium regime in which subharmonic temporal order survives inside deterministic chaos. Here we revisit this phenomenology from the viewpoint of classical nonlinear dynamics. Banded chaotic attractors consist of a finite number of chaotic sectors cyclically permuted by stroboscopic evolution, allowing discrete subharmonic spectral components to coexist with a broadband chaotic continuum. Exemplified through the driven Duffing oscillator and the logistic map, this structure naturally reproduces the characteristic signatures of time-semicrystalline dynamics. Within this framework, periodic subharmonic motion can enter chaos through the familiar period-doubling cascade while retaining a well-defined temporal skeleton governed by the universal Feigenbaum scaling. Temporal order within chaos can also reorganize or collapse through distinct mechanisms, producing continuous or abrupt transitions that may be intertwined with symmetry changes. These results connect time-semicrystal phenomenology with established structures of dissipative nonlinear dynamics, showing that its essential ingredients already arise in standard nonlinear systems and providing a simple framework for extending and testing the paradigm in more complex, many-body, and experimental settings.
tldr: The paper reinterprets time-semicrystalline order as a manifestation of banded chaotic attractors in classical driven nonlinear systems.
motivation: Recent work introduced time semicrystals as driven nonequilibrium regimes where subharmonic temporal order survives inside deterministic chaos, motivating a classical nonlinear-dynamics perspective.
method: The author analyzes banded chaotic attractors, illustrated with the driven Duffing oscillator and the logistic map, linking subharmonic spectral components to cyclic permutation of chaotic sectors and period-doubling routes to chaos.
result: Subharmonic temporal order can coexist with broadband chaos, follow Feigenbaum scaling, and reorganize or collapse through continuous or abrupt transitions that may involve symmetry changes.
conclusion: Time-semicrystal phenomenology arises naturally in standard dissipative nonlinear systems, providing a simple framework for extending and testing the paradigm in many-body and experimental settings.

title: Silmarils-mv: Information-Theoretically Secure Multi-Verifier Signatures With Dealer-Free Key Issuance And Linear Aggregation For Permissioned Blockchains
authors: Khadijeh Bagheri, Hassan Khodaiemehr, Chen Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Permissioned blockchains authenticate transactions, votes and quorum certificates with computationally secure signatures, and post-quantum replacements inflate consensus traffic by orders of magnitude. Information-theoretic alternatives have required a trusted authority, quantum channels, per-signature interaction, or single-use keys with bounded transfer. We present SILMARILS-MV, a multi-verifier unconditionally secure signature in which a signature is the vector [MATH] and each verifier holds a secret functional [MATH] derived from virtual anchors [MATH] that nobody learns. Against unbounded adversaries corrupting up to [MATH] verifiers and any signers, and observing every decision, an honest verifier accepts a forged or invalid signature with probability at most [MATH], a bound that is tight in its leading term. The scheme is strongly unforgeable, non-repudiable, transferable across unboundedly many hops, and linearly aggregatable. Keys are issued by the validators through perfectly secure MPC for [MATH], without broadcast. To scale, we let the committee itself sign: in threshold notarization, finality certificates have constant size [MATH] bytes and per-validator issuance cost no longer depends on [MATH]. Arbiter-verified keys give clients 32-byte signatures, robust redistribution supports membership changes and share refresh, and verifiers can be enrolled retroactively. A certificate verifies in 2.4 microseconds. In an analytic normal-case model at 1000 validators, threshold notarization needs 71 KiB of authentication traffic per validator per block, 22x less than ML-DSA-44 for admitted verifiers. In a Rust HotStuff prototype with 100 validators, SILMARILS-MV commits 2.8x more transactions per second than ML-DSA-44 with 67x less cryptographic CPU, and Monte-Carlo attacks match the bounds.
tldr: SILMARILS-MV is an information-theoretically secure multi-verifier signature scheme for permissioned blockchains with dealer-free key issuance and linear aggregation.
motivation: Permissioned blockchains rely on computationally secure signatures, and post-quantum replacements greatly increase consensus traffic; existing information-theoretic alternatives require trusted authorities, quantum channels, interaction, or single-use keys.
method: The scheme represents signatures as vectors and gives each verifier a secret functional derived from virtual anchors, with keys issued via perfectly secure MPC and supports threshold notarization, robust redistribution, and linear aggregation.
result: It achieves a tight forgery bound against unbounded adversaries corrupting up to a threshold of verifiers, provides strong unforgeability, non-repudiation, transferability, and aggregation, verifies certificates in 2.4 microseconds, and in a Rust HotStuff prototype commits 2.8x more transactions per second with 67x less cryptographic CPU than ML-DSA-44.
conclusion: The work offers a practical unconditionally secure signature alternative for permissioned blockchains, though it lies outside the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems focus areas.

title: Quantum Evolution Networks Learn Long-Time Coherent Dynamics In Driven Spin Registers
authors: Puran Li, Condon Lau, Xiu-Hao Deng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting and controlling driven quantum systems requires access to dynamics across physical parameters, initial states, and evolution times. A reusable neural model must capture this dependence while preserving unitary structure and maintaining accuracy over long-time coherent evolution. Here we introduce Quantum Evolution Networks (QENs), which map physical parameters and time to complete propagators for periodically driven three-spin registers. Shared networks learn unitary one-period propagators and compatible within-period paths, enabling predictions through known periodic composition without query-specific numerical integration. For transverse driving, the fifth-percentile fidelity, minimized over input states and sampled times, is 0.9947 over 24 periods on 256 held-out configurations. A leading-order analysis of spectrally resolved endpoint residuals predicts multicycle process error more accurately than quadratic or spectrum-averaged estimates. Interventions at matched single-period infidelity produce orders-of-magnitude differences in multicycle infidelity, demonstrating the importance of residual orientation. Compatible component replacements identify how endpoint and within-period approximations limit reconstruction accuracy. These results establish a reusable neural representation of the studied propagator families and connect its learned residual structure to its observed long-time reliability.
tldr: A neural network model called Quantum Evolution Networks learns to predict long-time coherent dynamics of periodically driven three-spin registers with high fidelity.
motivation: Predicting driven quantum dynamics across parameters and times is challenging; a reusable neural model could avoid query-specific numerical integration and preserve unitary structure.
method: QENs map physical parameters and time to complete propagators by learning one-period propagators and within-period paths, using shared networks and periodic composition.
result: Achieves fifth-percentile fidelity 0.9947 over 24 periods on held-out configurations; analysis of residual structure predicts multicycle process error and shows importance of residual orientation.
conclusion: The work establishes a reusable neural representation for propagator families and links learned residual structure to long-time reliability, with implications for quantum control.

title: Near-field Maps Of Topological Edge States Of Molecular Aggregates
authors: Aritra Mishra, Sidhartha Nayak, Alexander Eisfeld
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-assembled two-dimensional molecular aggregates provide a versatile platform for engineering excitonic states, including topologically nontrivial edge states. However, these edge-states are difficult to probe optically: they have weak far-field transition strengths, and far-field spectra do not reveal whether an excitation is localized at the edge. For an aggregate consisting of two sublattices of molecules with genuinely complex transition dipoles, we show that spatially resolved near-field spectroscopy encodes the full spatial structure of these states. The resulting near-field maps do not mirror the site populations, but instead exhibit strongly nonuniform, interference-like features. We demonstrate that a convolutional neural network can reconstruct the complex expansion coefficients of the eigenstates from these maps, and that this reconstruction is robust against substantial random noise.
tldr: The paper shows that near-field spectroscopy can spatially resolve topological edge states in molecular aggregates and that a CNN can reconstruct eigenstate coefficients from these maps.
motivation: Topological edge states in molecular aggregates are hard to probe optically because their far-field transition strengths are weak and far-field spectra do not reveal spatial localization.
method: The authors model a two-sublattice molecular aggregate with complex transition dipoles and compute spatially resolved near-field maps, then train a convolutional neural network to reconstruct complex eigenstate expansion coefficients from those maps.
result: Near-field maps exhibit strongly nonuniform interference-like features that do not simply mirror site populations, and the CNN reconstruction is robust against substantial random noise.
conclusion: Spatially resolved near-field spectroscopy combined with machine learning provides a route to characterize topological edge states in molecular aggregates, though the work is outside the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid-systems research directions.

title: Cross-coupled Photon Avalanche Drives Room-temperature Intrinsic Optical Bistability
authors: Eva Conour, Jacob Wojcik, Jory Sanders, Abigale Puccini, Trey Stephens-Cherry, Artiom Skripka
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optically bistable materials promise technological advances in optical information processing, memristive devices, and multiparametric sensing. However, optical bistability is predominantly observed under cryogenic conditions or is governed by subtle thermo-optical nonlinearities. Here, we report on Ho3+-activated nanocrystals that exhibit cavity-free intrinsic optical bistability (IOB) at ambient conditions. Non-thermal IOB stems from a cross-coupled photon avalanche (XPA) mechanism enabled by a low-phonon-energy double-perovskite host, which reduces nonradiative losses and facilitates excited-state population via XPA, even when the pump intensity is below threshold. Time-resolved luminescence measurements support the proposed XPA, as evidenced by a double-rise profile consistent with two reservoir states interlocked in energy looping. IOB with high-contrast photoswitching (up to 46 dB) is observed at room temperature across multiple visible emission lines, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing and compatibility with common detectors. IOB is preserved across nano- to microscale crystals and different double-perovskite compositions, broadly enabling information photonics and advanced sensing.
tldr: Ho3+-activated double-perovskite nanocrystals exhibit cavity-free, non-thermal intrinsic optical bistability at room temperature via a cross-coupled photon avalanche mechanism, enabling high-contrast all-optical switching.
motivation: Optical bistability is typically restricted to cryogenic operation or relies on weak thermo-optical effects, limiting its use for room-temperature photonic information processing and memristive or sensing applications.
method: Lanthanide-doped nanocrystals grown in a low-phonon-energy double-perovskite host were characterized by time-resolved luminescence, revealing a double-rise profile consistent with two interlocked reservoir states, and their bistable response was probed across visible emission lines, crystal sizes, and host compositions.
result: The authors observe intrinsic optical bistability at ambient conditions with photoswitching contrast up to 46 dB, preserved from nano- to microscale crystals and across several double-perovskite compositions, with the behavior attributed to a non-thermal cross-coupled photon avalanche.
conclusion: The platform offers a broadly tunable, cavity-free route to room-temperature optical bistability for wavelength-division multiplexing, information photonics, and multiparametric sensing.

title: Real-space Construction And Selection Rules Of Center-of-mass Momentum Eigenstates In Two-dimensional Many-body Lattices
authors: Ling Lin, Yongguan Ke, Chaohong Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comprehensive framework for the real-space construction of center-of-mass (c.m.) momentum eigenstates in two-dimensional (2D) quantum many-body systems. Unlike standard momentum-space approaches, our real-space formalism explicitly captures the non-uniformity of cyclic subspace dimensions, which are fundamentally governed by the spatial symmetries of the many-body configurations and particle statistics. We demonstrate that performing 2D real-space translations on multi-particle states naturally induces non-trivial translation phase factors associated with the characters of these stabilizer subgroups, leading to a renormalization of permissible momentum values. Notably, we identify an anomalous cross-dimensional momentum coupling in highly symmetric particle distributions, where the permissible momentum values in one direction are strictly constrained by those in the perpendicular direction. We emphasize the algorithmic necessity of this coupling, as neglecting it leads to missing or duplicated basis states in numerical implementations. Concrete examples are provided to demonstrate the practical implementation and physical consequences of this framework.
tldr: The paper develops a real-space framework for constructing center-of-mass momentum eigenstates in two-dimensional many-body lattices and derives selection rules induced by spatial symmetries and particle statistics.
motivation: Standard momentum-space methods do not explicitly handle non-uniform cyclic subspace dimensions in finite many-body lattices, motivating a real-space construction that captures symmetry-induced constraints.
method: The authors analyze 2D real-space translations on multi-particle states, identify stabilizer subgroup characters that renormalize allowed momenta, and derive an anomalous cross-dimensional momentum coupling for highly symmetric configurations.
result: The formalism reveals nontrivial translation phase factors, momentum-value renormalization, and cross-dimensional constraints that must be included to avoid missing or duplicated basis states in numerical implementations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and symmetry-aware basis-construction algorithm for 2D many-body lattice problems, though it is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Distortion-Rate Outage Probability For Non-ergodic Classes Of Sources
authors: Dongmin Park, Ibrahim Abou-Faycal, Razane Tajeddine
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The concept of outage has been commonly used in the context of transmission rates over non-ergodic channels. For those channels, one channel state or realization may be encountered for the whole transmission duration of a codeword. In the dual setting of source coding and whenever source statistics are not ergodic, we define in this work the notion of outage; we discuss related properties, consider the special case of compact source classes and provide examples.
tldr: The paper introduces a notion of outage for lossy source coding when source statistics are non-ergodic, defining distortion-rate outage probability and analyzing properties for compact source classes.
motivation: Outage concepts are well established for transmission over non-ergodic channels, where a single channel realization persists over a codeword; the authors argue a dual notion is missing on the source-coding side when source statistics are not ergodic.
method: The authors define distortion-rate outage probability for non-ergodic source classes, derive related structural properties, specialize to compact source classes, and provide illustrative examples.
result: Properties of the proposed outage quantity are established and explicit characterizations are given for compact source classes, supported by worked examples.
conclusion: The work extends the outage framework from non-ergodic channel coding to the dual source-coding setting, providing a vocabulary and basic theory for non-ergodic rate-distortion problems, though with no quantum information component.

title: Quasideterminants And Differential Realizations Of W-algebras
authors: Daniil Getta Sergey Derkachov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study the Hamiltonian reduction, used in constructing finite rectangular [MATH]-algebras, of the big-cell differential realization of [MATH]. We establish an intrinsic factorization of the reduced differential realization, identifying its Yangian action with the coproduct action on a tensor product of [MATH] evaluation differential realizations of [MATH]. Corner quasideterminants provide the essential noncommutative mechanism through which Hamiltonian reduction transforms the higher-rank differential realization into a factorized lower-rank Yangian action.
tldr: The paper studies Hamiltonian reduction of the big-cell differential realization of a quantum group to obtain finite rectangular W-algebras, showing the reduced realization factorizes via corner quasideterminants into a Yangian coproduct acting on a tensor product of evaluation modules.
motivation: Finite W-algebras and their Yangian symmetries are central to integrable models and representation theory, but the noncommutative mechanism by which Hamiltonian reduction factorizes higher-rank differential realizations is not fully understood.
method: The authors perform Hamiltonian reduction on the big-cell differential realization and use corner quasideterminants as the algebraic tool to identify an intrinsic factorization of the reduced realization.
result: The reduced differential realization factorizes, and its Yangian action is identified with the coproduct action on a tensor product of evaluation differential realizations of the underlying algebra.
conclusion: Corner quasideterminants provide the essential noncommutative mechanism converting higher-rank differential realizations into factorized lower-rank Yangian actions, clarifying the structure of finite rectangular W-algebras.

title: Coherent Axion Electrodynamics In Osiris: A Counter-propagating Axion-photon Parametric Instability
authors: Miles Radford, Pablo Bilbao, Thomas Grismayer, Luis Silva, Robert Bingham, Subir Sarkar, Gianluca Gregori
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a coherent axion-electrodynamics extension of the OSIRIS particle-in-cell code and use it to identify and benchmark a parametric axion-photon instability supported by two equal counter-propagating electromagnetic pumps. The module evolves a cell-centered axion field together with a separately stored first-order electromagnetic response on the native staggered OSIRIS grid. Re-examining the previously proposed strictly co-linear branch shows that it is removed when the axion-Maxwell equations are reduced consistently. A closely related standing-wave geometry, however, supports a distinct Floquet instability. We derive the coupled Floquet problem for an equal-amplitude counter-propagating pump pair and obtain a reduced analytic growth rate and cutoff for the dominant long-wavelength envelope branch. For an axion mass-to-pump-frequency ratio of 0.06 and a per-beam vector-potential amplitude of 0.3, simulations at coupling strengths of 0.60, 0.80, and 1.00 reproduce both the growth-rate spectrum and the coupling-dependent instability boundary. The reduced theory predicts envelope-mode cutoffs of 8.44, 10.80, and 13.23, while OSIRIS finds exponential growth through modes 8, 10, and 13, respectively, with the next resolved modes stable. The electromagnetic diagnostics additionally resolve exponentially growing sidebands at twice the pump wavenumber, while the zero-wavenumber electric component exhibits no sustained growth, as expected for the unstable Floquet eigenvector. The agreement provides an end-to-end benchmark of the coherent axion-electromagnetic coupling and demonstrates that parametric growth of the axion field is present in a two-beam pump geometry.
tldr: The authors extend the OSIRIS particle-in-cell code with a coherent axion-electrodynamics module and use it to identify and benchmark a Floquet-type parametric axion-photon instability driven by two counter-propagating electromagnetic pumps.
motivation: Axion-photon mixing in plasmas is a proposed search channel for ultralight dark matter, and previous claims of a strictly co-linear parametric instability need to be checked with a consistent numerical treatment of the axion-Maxwell equations.
method: A cell-centered axion field and a separately stored first-order electromagnetic response are implemented on the staggered OSIRIS grid; the coupled Floquet problem for an equal-amplitude counter-propagating pump pair is reduced analytically to an envelope growth rate and cutoff, then compared against PIC simulations at three coupling strengths.
result: The reduced theory predicts envelope-mode cutoffs of 8.44, 10.80 and 13.23 for couplings 0.60, 0.80 and 1.00, while simulations show exponential growth through modes 8, 10 and 13 respectively, with sidebands at twice the pump wavenumber and no sustained growth of the zero-wavenumber electric component.
conclusion: The previously proposed strictly co-linear branch is removed under a consistent reduction, but a standing-wave two-beam geometry supports a genuine Floquet instability, and the agreement between reduced theory and simulation provides an end-to-end benchmark of coherent axion-electromagnetic coupling.

title: Averages Of Traces And Ratios Of Characteristic Polynomials Of Random Unitary Matrices
authors: Ada Bendel, Rhys Cahill, John Brian Conrey, Gregor Harrison Barraclough, Ayesha Irfan, Nina Claire Snaith, Leonid Tyulenev
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we explore the extent to which the Ratios Theorem for averages over [MATH], with respect to Haar measure, of ratios of characteristic polynomials can be used to evaluate averages of traces of unitary matrices. We derive concrete expressions for all averages involving up to 4 traces, valid for any matrix size, [MATH]. We also calculate the so-called zero-swap and one-swap contributions to an average with any number of traces, which amounts to determining general trace moments in a range double the size of the renowned result of Diaconis and Shahshahani. The expression is tractable enough to use in applications, for example to determine the parameter range where certain trace averages assume negative values.
tldr: The paper studies averages of traces and ratios of characteristic polynomials of Haar-random unitary matrices using the Ratios Theorem.
motivation: The authors aim to determine how far the Ratios Theorem can be used to compute averages of traces of random unitary matrices and to extend known trace moment results.
method: They derive explicit expressions for averages involving up to four traces for arbitrary matrix size and compute zero-swap and one-swap contributions for arbitrary numbers of traces.
result: They obtain tractable general trace moment formulas extending the Diaconis-Shahshahani range by a factor of two and identify parameter ranges where certain trace averages become negative.
conclusion: The work provides mathematical results in random matrix theory, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Effective Multiplicative Ergodic Theorems For Banach Space Cocycles
authors: Adam Zaidan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The multiplicative ergodic theorem (MET) describes the asymptotic growth rates of [MATH]-volumes under the iterates of an operator cocycle, i.e., compositions of operators driven by a stationary process, organizing the underlying space into equivariant filtrations or splittings into so called Oseledets subspaces. For operator cocycles in finite dimensions, and more generally in Hilbert spaces, one can control the geometry of the Oseledets subspaces given by the MET via the convergence rates of finite-time volume growth data. This makes the MET "effective" for matrix and Hilbert-space operator cocycles. We extend this effective theory to cocycles of Banach-space operators, obtaining quantitative angle estimates that are new even in the finite-dimensional setting. We take a sequential approach \`{a} la Raghunathan and Ruelle, allowing us to separate the geometric argument of the MET from measure-theoretic considerations. This permits weaker cocycle measurability hypotheses for the non-invertible and semi-invertible METs on a broad class of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones. As an application, we establish the MET for transfer operator cocycles on [MATH] associated with jointly measurable random Lasota-Yorke maps.
tldr: The paper develops an effective (quantitative) multiplicative ergodic theorem for Banach-space operator cocycles, giving explicit angle estimates between Oseledets subspaces.
motivation: Effective METs are known for matrix and Hilbert-space cocycles but not for general Banach spaces, where the geometry of Oseledets filtrations is harder to control quantitatively.
method: A sequential approach in the style of Raghunathan and Ruelle separates the geometric argument from measure-theoretic issues, yielding quantitative angle estimates under weaker measurability hypotheses, including nonseparable Banach spaces.
result: Quantitative angle estimates for Oseledets subspaces of Banach-space cocycles that are new even in finite dimensions, plus non-invertible and semi-invertible METs under weaker hypotheses and an MET for transfer operator cocycles of random Lasota–Yorke maps.
conclusion: The work extends effective multiplicative ergodic theory beyond Hilbert spaces and applies it to random transfer operators, but remains a pure ergodic-theory/dynamical-systems contribution.

title: Block Toeplitz Operators, Matrix Valued Truncated Toeplitz Operators, And Conjugations
authors: Rewayat Khan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we characterize the complex symmetry of block Toeplitz operators on the Hardy-Hilbert space H2(E) with conjugation C_{u,\lambda}, where E is a finite dimensional Hilbert space. We also extend the application of this conjugation to matrix valued truncated Toeplitz operators.
tldr: The paper characterizes complex symmetry (conjugation-based symmetry) of block Toeplitz operators acting on vector-valued Hardy-Hilbert spaces, extending the analysis to matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operators.
motivation: Complex symmetric operators form a broad class generalizing self-adjoint and normal structures; understanding when block and truncated Toeplitz operators are complex symmetric with respect to a given conjugation C_{u,λ} clarifies their spectral and structural properties.
method: Pure operator-theoretic analysis: the authors define a family of conjugations C_{u,λ} on H^2(E) for finite-dimensional E and derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the symbols for the corresponding block Toeplitz and matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operators to be complex symmetric.
result: Explicit symbol-level characterizations of C_{u,λ}-complex symmetry for block Toeplitz operators are obtained, and these conditions are carried over to matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operators on model spaces.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic functional-analytic framework for complex symmetry in vector-valued Toeplitz settings, but it remains a purely mathematical operator theory contribution with no direct bearing on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Deterministic Constructions Of Reed-Solomon Codes Beyond The Johnson Bound
authors: Abhranil Chatterjee, Sumanta Ghosh, Zeyu Guo, Rohit Gurjar, Roshan Raj
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a deterministic quasipolynomial-time construction of Reed-Solomon codes that are list-decodable beyond the Johnson radius. Specifically, for every [MATH] and all sufficiently large [MATH], we construct an [MATH] Reed-Solomon code of rate [MATH] over a field of size [MATH] that is [MATH] list-decodable. The construction runs in quasi-poly(nk) time. We also give a deterministic construction of [MATH]-MDS[MATH] Reed-Solomon codes for all integers [MATH], with the same asymptotic bounds on field size and construction time. In the constant-rate regime, our field-size bound substantially improves the bound of [MATH] achieved by Roth's construction (Roth, IEEE TIT 2022). Our constructions exploit a connection to polynomial identity testing for read-once determinants, together with the quasipolynomial isolating-weight construction of Gurjar and Thierauf for linear matroid intersection (Gurjar and Thierauf, STOC 2017 and Computational Complexity 2020).
tldr: This paper gives deterministic quasipolynomial-time constructions of Reed-Solomon codes that are list-decodable beyond the Johnson radius, improving field-size bounds over prior work.
motivation: Reed-Solomon codes are central in classical coding theory, and list-decodability beyond the Johnson bound is a longstanding challenge; existing constructions often rely on randomness or have suboptimal field-size bounds.
method: The authors connect the construction to polynomial identity testing for read-once determinants and use the quasipolynomial isolating-weight construction of Gurjar and Thierauf for linear matroid intersection.
result: They construct Reed-Solomon codes with rate and field size beating Roth's construction in the constant-rate regime, and also obtain deterministic constructions of k-MDS Reed-Solomon codes.
conclusion: The work advances classical coding theory and algebraic complexity, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Randomization To Balance Performance Under Nominal And Compromised Communication
authors: Colton Hill, Brandon Collins, Philip N. Brown
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well-known that under nominal communication, where agents are able to share information with one another, game-theoretic methods provide system-level performance guarantees in multiagent cyber-physical human systems such as distributed resource allocation. However, approaches that depend on communication are frequently not robust when communication is compromised. While randomized decision-making can prevent arbitrarily poor outcomes under compromised communication, these performance guarantees often do not improve when communication abilities are restored. Thus, it remains unclear whether a single approach can perform well under nominal communication and remain robust under compromised communication. In this paper, we study whether a system operator can inform agents about how much they should randomize their choice when selecting actions in order to balance performance across both settings. We show that for any scenario (e.g., a multiagent resource allocation instance), there exists a level of randomization where nominal efficiency is near-optimal while compromised efficiency is strictly positive. We then show that this guarantee weakens as agents must choose between increasingly many resources. These results provide an initial step toward understanding randomization as a tool for robust performance across communication settings.
tldr: The paper studies how a system operator can set a randomization level for agents in multiagent cyber-physical human systems so that performance is near-optimal under nominal communication while remaining strictly positive when communication is compromised.
motivation: Game-theoretic multiagent methods guarantee good system-level performance when agents can communicate, but degrade badly under compromised communication, and purely randomized strategies that are robust in that regime do not improve once communication is restored.
method: The authors analyze multiagent resource allocation instances and prove existence of a randomization level balancing nominal and compromised efficiency, then extend the analysis to settings with growing numbers of resources.
result: For any scenario there exists a randomization level achieving near-optimal nominal efficiency with strictly positive compromised efficiency, but this guarantee weakens as the number of resources agents must choose among increases.
conclusion: Randomization is presented as an initial tool for robust performance across communication settings, framing a trade-off between nominal efficiency and adversarial robustness in multiagent systems.

title: Embedding Large Pqc KEMs In IKEv2
authors: Daniel Herzinger, Marco Thomas, Tobias Handirk, Stefan-Lukas Gazdag, Daniel Loebenberger, Marian Margraf
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-quantum key encapsulation mechanisms carry public keys far larger than the established VPN handshake protocol IKEv2 was designed for. At the same time, its initial exchange comprising the public keys cannot be fragmented. In response, the IETF discusses a range of protocol adjustments, yet these proposals have never been compared in terms of their performance and stability under identical conditions. We systematically screened the IETF document corpus for such proposals, added three of our own (one using forward error correction and two using IKEv2 with QUIC, namely QUIKE and QUIKE with a composite key exchange), identified two specification gaps in existing acknowledgment drafts, and implemented all eight on the same open-source codebase. Measurements across different bandwidths, latencies, and packet loss rates, and with ML-KEM, FrodoKEM, and Classic McEliece, total 126 500 handshakes in 1296 different configurations and show that no mechanism fully compensates for the effect of the key size on performance. For Classic McEliece, no approach handles challenging conditions acceptably. The approaches either congest the link or take up to nearly two minutes per handshake on average. For ML-KEM and FrodoKEM, there are two ways forward: building on already standardized extensions or delegating the transport. The former requires the larger implementation change and needs further optimization, such as acknowledgment mechanisms or error-correcting codes, but grants continuity and compatibility. The latter can use a composite key exchange to avoid these drawbacks and achieve a faster, more resilient handshake and leaner implementation, with QUIKE-composite offering the best overall performance.
tldr: This paper systematically compares eight approaches for embedding large post-quantum KEM public keys into the IKEv2 VPN handshake protocol.
motivation: Post-quantum KEMs have much larger public keys than IKEv2 was designed to handle, and the initial exchange cannot be fragmented, creating performance and stability challenges.
method: The authors screen IETF proposals, add three of their own designs (including QUIKE and QUIKE-composite), implement all eight on a common open-source codebase, and measure 126,500 handshakes across 1,296 configurations with ML-KEM, FrodoKEM, and Classic McEliece.
result: No mechanism fully compensates for key-size effects; Classic McEliece remains impractical under challenging conditions, while for ML-KEM and FrodoKEM the best paths are standardized extensions or delegating transport, with QUIKE-composite performing best overall.
conclusion: For large PQ KEMs in IKEv2, transport delegation via QUIC with composite key exchange offers faster, more resilient handshakes and leaner implementation than acknowledgment or FEC-based extensions.

title: Afra: Age-Threshold Frame-Based Random Access For Timely Communication In Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Fang Liu Jiedan Tan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Timely state updates are essential for coordination and monitoring in multi-agent systems, such as teams of mobile robots exchanging state information. When agents share a wireless channel, collisions and slow convergence of distributed access schemes can degrade information freshness over finite operating periods. This paper proposes age-threshold frame-based random access (AFRA), a distributed medium access control protocol for minimizing age of information (AoI). Once its age reaches a threshold, an agent starts a local frame with a mandatory transmission and, if unsuccessful, makes one further attempt at a uniformly selected remaining slot. Each attempt carries a freshly generated update. AFRA requires only local state and acknowledgment feedback, with shared slot boundaries but independently timed local frames. We prove almost-sure convergence from any legal initial state to collision-free periodic operation when the frame length [MATH] and age threshold [MATH] satisfy [MATH], where [MATH] is the number of agents. We also derive closed-form expressions for steady-state throughput, average AoI, and average peak AoI. Simulations demonstrate that AFRA combines rapid convergence at small age thresholds with lower window-averaged AoI than the existing age-aware random access schemes evaluated in this study.
tldr: AFRA is a distributed frame-based random access protocol for minimizing age of information in multi-agent wireless systems.
motivation: Timely state updates are important for coordination in multi-agent systems, but shared wireless channels suffer from collisions and slow distributed access convergence.
method: The protocol triggers a local frame when an agent's age reaches a threshold, uses a mandatory transmission plus one retry in a uniformly chosen remaining slot, and relies only on local state and acknowledgments.
result: The authors prove almost-sure convergence to collision-free periodic operation under a condition relating frame length, age threshold, and number of agents, and derive steady-state throughput and average/peak AoI expressions.
conclusion: AFRA improves convergence and window-averaged AoI compared with existing age-aware random access schemes in simulations, but the work is classical networking and not quantum information research.

title: Polyhedral Ris Architecture With Quantum-Assisted Facet Selection For Uniform Coverage
authors: Halim Yanikomeroglu Noha Hassan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) direct coverage toward moving user equipment (UE), but practical deployments involve discrete phase control, uncertain facet positions, and UE mobility, which require the problem to be re-solved continually. We consider these challenges for the chamfered hexagonal polyhedral RIS, which provides nearly uniform coverage. With both incidence and departure angles, we bound in closed form the gain loss of its best facet relative to the best possible reflecting facet, include the known b-bit quantization loss, and extend the bound to joint random mounting errors of all facets. For a precoded multi-user downlink, each facet-selection subproblem of the max-min rate design is shown to be an exact quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, suited to repeated time-constrained solving. The deployment of the base station in relation to the RIS allows the polyhedral surface to bring down the percentage of dead zones in vertical planar panels from 77% to 0.3% and increase the minimum rate by 34% relative to the STAR panel. The simulated annealing algorithm finds the optimum solution in 95% of the cases. The quantum approximation algorithm fails to do so.
tldr: This paper designs a polyhedral reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) architecture and formulates facet selection as a QUBO problem for quantum-assisted optimization, but its focus is wireless network coverage rather than quantum information science.
motivation: Practical RIS deployments face discrete phase control, uncertain facet positions, and user mobility, requiring repeated optimization to maintain uniform coverage.
method: The authors bound gain loss for a chamfered hexagonal polyhedral RIS, formulate each facet-selection subproblem in a max-min rate design as an exact QUBO, and compare simulated annealing with a quantum approximation algorithm.
result: The polyhedral RIS reduces dead zones from 77% to 0.3% and improves minimum rate by 34% relative to a STAR panel; simulated annealing finds the optimum in 95% of cases while the quantum approximation algorithm fails to do so.
conclusion: Polyhedral RIS with QUBO-based facet selection is effective for uniform wireless coverage, but quantum-assisted optimization did not outperform classical simulated annealing in this setting.

title: Research Profiles And The Mathematical Landscape: A Grassroots Proposal For Mathematics With Ai
authors: Helmut H. W. Hofer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repeated mathematical work with AI leaves behind corrections, failed arguments, and sometimes useful ways of asking questions. I propose keeping these in a research profile that the mathematician develops and controls. The profile marks parts of the mathematical landscape according to the researcher's understanding and makes those markings available to later work with AI. This suggests experiments with individual profiles, shared readings of papers, and graduate education. It also raises mathematical questions about the landscape itself: its connections, distances, and changes under discovery. I describe two examples, searching for branches of mathematics with a common base and recovering useful questions from the history of Floer theory. The aim is to give mathematicians something to try and a part in deciding how mathematical AI develops.
tldr: The paper proposes that mathematicians maintain personal 'research profiles' recording corrections, failed arguments, and productive question framings, which can be shared with AI systems to shape future mathematical work.
motivation: Repeated AI-assisted mathematical work generates useful byproducts—corrections, dead ends, and fruitful question formulations—that are currently discarded rather than captured and reused.
method: A conceptual/grassroots proposal illustrated by two case studies: identifying branches of mathematics sharing a common base, and recovering useful open questions from the history of Floer theory.
result: The proposal outlines experiments with individual profiles, shared readings of papers, and graduate education, and poses mathematical questions about the structure of the 'mathematical landscape' (connections, distances, change under discovery).
conclusion: Mathematicians should have a controlling stake in how mathematical AI develops, and research profiles offer a concrete mechanism for that participation.

title: Optimal Graphon Control Of Collective Dynamics
authors: Brandon Su Joseph K. Miller
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study optimal control of non-linear graphon dynamics in which the interaction kernel itself is the control. Motivated by opinion formation in social networks, we ask how changing who influences whom can steer a population toward a desired outcome. We develop a framework using interaction kernels with bounded variation in the receiver label, providing compactness while accommodating finite networks. We prove existence of an optimal pair and show that finite-agent approximations recover the continuum optimal value under successive refinement of the network and initial data, with subsequential convergence of suitably chosen discrete optimizers. Numerical experiments use neural networks to approximate optimal controls for bounded-confidence and graphon Kuramoto dynamics, illustrating how changes in interactions can prevent fragmentation and promote synchronization.
tldr: The paper develops optimal control for nonlinear graphon dynamics where the interaction kernel is the control variable, motivated by opinion formation and synchronization in networks.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how modifying influence patterns in large networked populations can steer collective behavior toward desired outcomes such as preventing fragmentation or promoting synchronization.
method: They formulate optimal control over interaction kernels with bounded variation in the receiver label, prove existence of an optimal pair, and establish convergence of finite-agent approximations to the continuum optimal value.
result: Numerical experiments approximate optimal controls using neural networks for bounded-confidence opinion dynamics and graphon Kuramoto dynamics, showing that interaction changes can prevent fragmentation and promote synchronization.
conclusion: The framework provides a mathematically rigorous continuum control approach for collective network dynamics, with finite-network approximation guarantees and illustrative neural-network solutions.

title: Fisher Information And The Minimum Mean-Square Error For Locating Closely Spaced Point Sources
authors: Chuling Wen, Jian Lu, Qingtang Jiang, Charles K. Chui
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the optimal average error of locating closely spaced sources from noisy superpositions of a known smooth response with unknown complex coefficients. Relative phases control how changes in one location can be offset by the other unknowns, so local Fisher information alone does not determine the attainable error. For every fixed number [MATH] of sources with independent uniform phases, we prove matching Bayes risk bounds jointly in separation and noise, for all sufficiently small separations and all noise levels. Odd source counts have two risk regimes; even counts have an intermediate regime in which mean squared error is linear in the noise standard deviation. A projected least-squares estimator attains these orders without knowing the phases or the prior density. Bounded nonuniform phase laws preserve the orders under stated support conditions, whereas priors concentrated near poorly identified configurations can change the exponents. A common finite comparison yields both a global inverse bound and paths controlled by the original prior. These give sufficient conditions under which the risk has the order of the pointwise capped Cram\'er--Rao bound, and a lower-tail calculation explains the power and logarithmic regimes. We also give conditional guarantees when the cluster center, separation, and source count are unknown, with an additional low-noise requirement for count selection. A calibrated covariance factor model illustrates the same criterion beyond source localization.
tldr: The paper derives matching Bayes-risk bounds, jointly in separation and noise, for estimating the locations of closely spaced point sources with unknown complex amplitudes and random phases, showing when the risk follows a capped Cramér–Rao scaling.
motivation: Local Fisher information is insufficient to determine achievable localization error when relative phases allow one source's displacement to be offset by other unknowns, so a global minimax analysis was needed.
method: The authors prove matching upper and lower bounds on average mean-square error for each fixed source count with uniform independent phases, and construct a projected least-squares estimator that attains the bounds without knowledge of phases or prior density.
result: Odd source counts yield two risk regimes, while even counts show an intermediate regime where mean-square error is linear in the noise standard deviation; bounded nonuniform phase laws preserve the orders under support conditions, whereas concentrated priors can alter the exponents.
conclusion: The analysis gives sufficient conditions under which localization risk matches the pointwise capped Cramér–Rao bound, and extends to unknown cluster center, separation, and source count, with a calibrated covariance factor model illustrating the criterion.

title: Label-Budgeted Attribute Inference From Protected Features In Edge-Cloud Split Multimodal LLMs
authors: Junguang Yao, Peichun Hua, Hanxiu Zhang, Yue Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Edge-cloud split inference runs the early layers of a multimodal large language model (MLLM) on a device and sends intermediate features to a server to complete the task. While keeping raw images local is often perceived as a privacy benefit, an honest-but-curious server can still infer sensitive attributes, such as age, gender, and race, from the received features. Existing protections intervene at the input, transmitted representation, or model's responses, but their native evaluations rely on final-response refusals or fixed-classifier failures, which underestimate an adaptive server's capabilities. To address this, we propose a label-budgeted attribute-inference framework that measures representation-level privacy through a recovery curve: the share of the unprotected leakage the server recovers as a function of its labeled-sample budget, from zero (a classifier trained on unprotected features) to a full labeled set. Our evaluation across two popular MLLMs reveals two critical findings. First, in unprotected pipelines, intermediate features leak all three attributes regardless of the split depth. Second, even when protection mechanisms are deployed across different stages, sensitive information remains recoverable under limited label budgets. For example, Safe-LLaVA removes biometric content from the model's responses, but from the features it transmits in split inference, 20 labeled samples per class recover 75-85% of the unprotected leakage. This work provides a label-budgeted measure of feature-level privacy for split MLLM inference and motivates defenses that act on the transmitted representation.
tldr: The paper proposes a label-budgeted framework to quantify attribute leakage (age, gender, race) from intermediate features transmitted in edge-cloud split inference of multimodal LLMs.
motivation: Splitting an MLLM between device and server is often assumed to protect privacy by keeping raw images local, but an honest-but-curious server may still recover sensitive attributes from the transmitted representations, and existing evaluations understate adaptive adversaries.
method: The authors introduce a recovery-curve metric measuring the fraction of unprotected leakage an adversary recovers as a function of its labeled-sample budget, and benchmark several protection mechanisms across two MLLMs and multiple split depths.
result: Unprotected pipelines leak all three attributes at any split depth, and even protected pipelines (e.g., Safe-LLaVA) allow 75-85% of unprotected leakage to be recovered with only 20 labeled samples per class.
conclusion: Feature-level privacy in split MLLM inference requires defenses that act directly on the transmitted representation rather than on inputs or outputs.

title: Radical: Reconfiguration-Aware Direct-Connect Ai Cluster Using Spatial-and-Wavelength Selective Switching
authors: Brett George, Weiyang Wang, Yuyang Wang, Zhenguo Wu, S. C. Mancas, Xiang Meng, Manya Ghobadi, Keren Bergman
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present RADICAL, the silicon-photonic-enabled Reconfiguration-Aware Direct-Connect AI Cluster that integrates a custom spatial-and-wavelength selective switch (SWSS) with the Linux network stack. RADICAL deploys a packaged 4x4x4[MATH] microring-based SWSS into a four-GPU-server cluster using standard SFP28 optical transceivers, and a reconfiguration-aware host-networking interface to demonstrate a direct-connect reconfigurable optical fabric. The SWSS provides dynamic spatial and wavelength routing with 3.2-6.8 dB path loss, average wavelength and spatial crosstalk isolation exceeding 25 dB, and error-free 25 Gbps signal recovery across routing paths. At the system level, RADICAL validates reconfiguration-aware operation through continuous bulk data transfers totaling 6.4 TBytes over 10 minutes. We further demonstrate multitenant AI training across reconfigurable link topologies, including four ResNet-18 instances and six nanoGPT instances, with the latter sustained for more than five hours.
tldr: RADICAL is a silicon-photonic reconfigurable optical fabric for direct-connect AI GPU clusters using a spatial-and-wavelength selective switch.
motivation: AI training clusters require flexible, high-bandwidth interconnects that can be reconfigured dynamically for multitenant and topology-dependent workloads.
method: The authors integrate a packaged 4x4x4 microring-based spatial-and-wavelength selective switch with standard SFP28 transceivers and a reconfiguration-aware Linux host-networking interface in a four-GPU-server cluster.
result: The system achieves 3.2–6.8 dB path loss, >25 dB crosstalk isolation, error-free 25 Gbps signal recovery, and sustains 6.4 TBytes of bulk transfers over 10 minutes while running multitenant ResNet-18 and nanoGPT training.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical reconfigurable optical fabric for AI clusters, but it is a classical photonic networking and systems contribution with no quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum network relevance.

title: Revealing And Mitigating Transmittance And Reflectance Errors In Integrating-Sphere Characterization Of High-Albedo Scattering Media
authors: Zhijie Xu, Ernesto Pini, Lorenzo Pattelli, Ioannis Papakonstantinou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate optical characterization of high-albedo scattering media is fundamentally limited by integrating-sphere measurement errors. Scattering events spatially redistribute photons, leading to lateral beam spread and angular divergence that bias measured reflectance and transmittance. Here, we investigate these deviations, which are quantified and interpreted by using the point spread function (PSF), guided by the radiative transfer equation. Experiments and Monte Carlo modelling show that the widely used external-mount integrating-sphere configuration introduces systematic, configuration-dependent errors that become pronounced when scattering-induced lateral spreading is substantial. Using a normalised PSF to quantify photon redistribution, we map the characteristic lateral spreading length across a broad [MATH] parameter space in the high-albedo limit, providing a basis for evaluating errors in specific measurement geometries. We further quantify the influence of measurement geometry and show that, in the pencil-beam limit, maintaining [MATH] reduces the discrepancy arising from the finite collection aperture to approximately {\percent}. In addition, we introduce an internal-mount integrating-sphere protocol that suppresses scattering-related losses and yields transmittance and reflectance measurements in good agreement with theoretical predictions. Overall, our work helps users of integrating-sphere measurements identify scattering-related errors and improve the reliability of transmittance and reflectance characterization across a wide range of application areas.
tldr: The paper quantifies and mitigates systematic errors in integrating-sphere measurements of reflectance and transmittance for high-albedo scattering media using a point-spread-function framework derived from the radiative transfer equation.
