motivation: Accurate optical characterization of highly scattering, high-albedo media is limited by scattering-induced lateral beam spread and angular divergence that bias external-mount integrating-sphere measurements.
method: The authors combine experiments with Monte Carlo modelling, introduce a normalized PSF to quantify photon redistribution and map the characteristic lateral spreading length over a broad parameter space, and propose an internal-mount integrating-sphere protocol.
result: External-mount configurations show configuration-dependent systematic errors that grow with lateral spreading; in the pencil-beam limit keeping a small aperture ratio reduces the collection-aperture discrepancy to about a few percent, and the internal-mount protocol yields transmittance and reflectance in good agreement with theory.
conclusion: The work provides practical guidance for identifying and suppressing scattering-related errors in integrating-sphere characterization of high-albedo media across many application areas.

title: Ozone Groups And Centers Of Two-parameter Quantum Heisenberg Algebras
authors: James G\'omez, H\'ector Su\'arez, Helbert Venegas
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be roots of unity with [MATH], and put [MATH] and [MATH]. Up to isomorphism, the two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras [MATH] are exactly the noetherian PI graded down-up algebras, so everything here holds for that whole class. The ozone group is [MATH], generated by conjugation by three normal elements, and the center is recovered from the fixed ring of the ozone group as the invariants of a cyclic group of order [MATH]. We give a presentation of the center as a hypersurface over a cyclic quotient surface singularity. It is regular exactly when [MATH] is a characteristic root, which disproves a conjecture of Chan, Gaddis, Won and Zhang, and Gorenstein exactly when [MATH], where [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH]; for [MATH], [MATH] it is not. We also decide when the fixed ring of the ozone group is Gorenstein and when [MATH] is Calabi--Yau, and show that the algebras with regular center have non-affine automorphisms and nonzero locally nilpotent derivations.
tldr: This paper studies algebraic and homological properties of two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras, including ozone groups, centers, Gorenstein conditions, and Calabi-Yau properties.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize the center and fixed-ring structure of two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras and to resolve conjectures about regularity and Gorenstein conditions in this algebraic class.
method: The paper uses ring-theoretic and invariant-theoretic techniques, analyzing ozone groups, fixed rings, hypersurface presentations, and cyclic quotient surface singularities.
result: It presents the center as a hypersurface over a cyclic quotient surface singularity, disproves a conjecture by Chan, Gaddis, Won and Zhang, and gives precise Gorenstein and Calabi-Yau criteria.
conclusion: The work advances the structure theory of quantum Heisenberg algebras and related graded down-up algebras but has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Generalization Of Gordon's Theorem To Arbitrary Winding Number
authors: M. Fenucci
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study minimizers of the Keplerian action functional with homogeneous potential of type [MATH] on periodic loops with fixed winding number [MATH]. This extends the classical theorems of Gordon and Venturelli, closing the previously open case [MATH], [MATH]. We show that the [MATH]-circular solution loses local minimality below the threshold [MATH], and that minimizers are collision-free above [MATH]. Combining these results with the existence of precessing periodic orbits in between, we obtain a full classification of the minimizer in terms of [MATH] and [MATH], which we also verify numerically for [MATH].
tldr: The paper classifies minimizers of the Keplerian action functional with homogeneous potentials on periodic loops of fixed winding number, extending Gordon's and Venturelli's classical theorems.
motivation: Gordon-type theorems characterize when action minimizers are collision-free; the case of low homogeneity exponent and nontrivial winding number had remained open and is needed for a complete variational picture of Keplerian-like systems.
method: Variational calculus on loop spaces with fixed winding number: local minimality analysis of the N-circular solution, threshold criteria for its loss of minimality, and existence arguments for precessing periodic orbits, supplemented by numerical verification.
result: The N-circular solution ceases to be locally minimal below an explicit threshold in the homogeneity exponent, minimizers are shown to be collision-free above it, and a full classification of minimizers in terms of the potential exponent and winding number is obtained.
conclusion: The work closes an open case in the Gordon–Venturelli program for Keplerian action functionals, yielding a complete minimizer classification that is confirmed numerically.

title: Polarized Ensemble Kalman Inversion: A Derivative-Free Method For Multimodal Inverse Problems With Non-asymptotic Analysis
authors: Jin-Long Wu Huchen Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inverse problems often admit multiple solutions consistent with the same noisy, indirect observations, especially with sparse data and/or strongly nonlinear forward models. Ensemble Kalman inversion (EKI) provides a robust, derivative-free framework to solve inverse problems, but its global empirical covariances couple all ensemble members across distinct solution modes, limiting its effectiveness for multimodal problems. We introduce polarized ensemble Kalman inversion (PEKI), which constructs distance-weighted local covariances for each ensemble member. This localization weakens contributions from distant, data-consistent regions and enables different clusters of ensemble members to evolve toward distinct solution modes. For the practical algorithm with finite ensemble size and polarization radius, we also establish non-asymptotic bounds and perform numerical studies, showing that cross-cluster effects decay exponentially with cluster separation relative to the polarization radius. For linear forward maps, we further establish particle-wise residual contraction and derive an exact cluster-mean decomposition that separates cross-cluster leakage, within-cluster gain variation, and observation perturbations. These results further motivate a one-step procedure for choosing the polarization radius by reusing stored forward-model evaluations. We studied the performance of PEKI on several numerical experiments, including low-dimensional nonconvex benchmarks, a problem equipped with many-mode landscape, and a high-dimensional inverse problem governed by Navier--Stokes equations. The results confirm the theoretical exponential decay of cross-cluster effects and show that PEKI can serve as a robust and derivative-free method for inverse problems with multiple solution modes.
tldr: The paper introduces polarized ensemble Kalman inversion (PEKI), a derivative-free method for multimodal inverse problems that uses distance-weighted local covariances to prevent cross-mode coupling in ensemble updates.
motivation: Standard ensemble Kalman inversion struggles with multimodal inverse problems because global empirical covariances couple ensemble members across distinct solution modes, limiting the method's ability to resolve multiple data-consistent solutions.
method: PEKI constructs a localized covariance for each ensemble member by down-weighting distant members according to a polarization radius, allowing clusters to evolve toward separate modes. The authors also derive non-asymptotic bounds and a linear forward-map decomposition, plus a one-step radius selection procedure.
result: Theoretical analysis shows cross-cluster effects decay exponentially with cluster separation relative to the polarization radius, and numerical experiments on nonconvex benchmarks, a many-mode problem, and a Navier-Stokes inverse problem confirm the predicted behavior.
conclusion: PEKI provides a robust derivative-free approach for multimodal inverse problems with theoretical support and practical radius-selection guidance, though it is outside the quantum information research areas targeted here.

title: Flexibility Of Topological Entropy And Factor Persistence In The $C^0$-Gromov Hausdorff Topology
authors: Jorge Crisostomo Richard Cubas
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every surjective topological dynamical system on a compact metric space can be approximated in the [MATH]-Gromov--Hausdorff topology by homeomorphisms with any prescribed topological entropy in [MATH], even when simultaneous approximation of its sets of invariant and ergodic measures is required. We also establish a rigidity result under uniform geometric bounds in a fixed dimension: for a homeomorphism of a closed, connected Riemannian manifold, topological stability in the sense of Gromov--Hausdorff guarantees its persistence as a factor of sufficiently close perturbations within the same geometric class. This persistence prevents topological entropy from decreasing and ensures that every invariant or ergodic measure of the original system admits a lift of the same type to the perturbed system.
tldr: The paper proves that surjective topological dynamical systems on compact metric spaces can be approximated in the C^0-Gromov-Hausdorff topology by homeomorphisms with arbitrarily prescribed topological entropy, and establishes a factor-persistence rigidity result on closed Riemannian manifolds.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how flexible topological entropy is under geometric-topological perturbations, and when invariant structures of a dynamical system persist under such perturbations.
method: Approximation arguments in the C^0-Gromov-Hausdorff topology combined with simultaneous control of invariant and ergodic measure sets; rigidity arguments using uniform geometric bounds in fixed dimension on closed connected Riemannian manifolds.
result: Every such system admits arbitrarily close homeomorphic perturbations with any prescribed entropy value, while within a fixed geometric class topological stability forces the original system to persist as a factor, preventing entropy decrease and lifting invariant/ergodic measures.
conclusion: Topological entropy is highly flexible under Gromov-Hausdorff approximation, yet rigid geometric constraints restore persistence of factors and measure-theoretic structure.

title: Perturbed Exponential Systems, Pattern-Dependent Shifted-Sinc Operators, And Matrix Symbols On Finite Unions Of Intervals
authors: Gohin Shaikh Samad Pierluigi Vellucci
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study perturbed exponential systems and unions of shifted frequency lattices through shifted-sinc operators and finite-dimensional fiberizations. For the auxiliary binary local-shift model, we identify the exact pattern-dependent invariant $[MATH][MATH]1\pm\rho_{\delta,s}[MATH]\delta=1/4$, a step pattern is governed by a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has vanishing lower bound, although every fixed periodic pattern remains invertible. We also combine exact bounds for structured patterns with a support-independent perturbation estimate, obtaining explicit stability neighborhoods. For finite unions of bounded intervals and finitely many shifted lattices, folding modulo one yields finitely many rectangular phase matrices whose singular values and ranks give the exact bounds and complete Riesz-sequence, frame, and Riesz-basis criteria. This framework also yields finite Hadamard constraints for periodic spectra and an exact reduction of rationally commensurate multirate sampling.
tldr: The paper develops shifted-sinc operator and matrix-symbol techniques to characterize stability, Riesz-sequence and frame properties of perturbed exponential systems and finite unions of shifted frequency lattices.
motivation: Perturbed exponential systems and unions of shifted lattices lack sharp, pattern-dependent stability criteria, and the authors aim to obtain exact, computable bounds for such systems.
method: They combine exact bounds for structured (periodic, step) patterns with a support-independent perturbation estimate, and use folding modulo one to reduce finite interval unions and shifted lattices to finitely many rectangular phase matrices whose singular values and ranks give the criteria.
result: They identify an exact pattern-dependent invariant 1±ρ_{δ,s}δ = 1/4 for a binary local-shift model, show a step pattern governed by a half-shifted Hilbert matrix has vanishing lower bound while every fixed periodic pattern stays invertible, and derive explicit stability neighborhoods plus Hadamard constraints and a reduction of commensurate multirate sampling.
conclusion: The framework yields complete Riesz-sequence, frame and Riesz-basis criteria for finite unions of intervals and finitely many shifted lattices, providing exact and computable stability analysis for such exponential systems.

title: Covariance-Informed Ensemble Score Filtering: Embedding Localized Covariance Geometry Into Score-Based Transport
authors: Siming Liang, Peter Jan van Leeuwen, Hristo G. Chipilski, Zezhong Zhang, Feng Bao, Guannan Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Background-error covariance models are central to atmospheric data assimilation because they spread partial observational information across space, variables, and dynamically coupled scales. Ensemble and variational methods exploit this covariance geometry efficiently, but their standard analysis formulations are largely built around Gaussian or locally quadratic approximations. Score-based ensemble filtering provides a framework for nonlinear distributional transport, but existing Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) formulations lack an intrinsic covariance-mediated pathway for propagating likelihood information from observed to unobserved state components. We introduce a covariance-informed ensemble score filter (CI-EnSF) that embeds localized forecast-error covariance geometry directly into the forward diffusion and reverse transport. The proposed forward diffusion is covariance-shaped in standardized state space and becomes isotropic under the corresponding control-variable transformation. This covariance structure continuously propagates observational information from observed to unobserved state components throughout the reverse transport analysis trajectory. Experiments with Lorenz-96 and surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) dynamics show a clear regime dependence. For linear observations, a well-tuned LETKF is more accurate, while CI-EnSF maintains stable cycling and effective covariance-mediated information propagation. Under strongly nonlinear observations and under climatological initialization, CI-EnSF achieves lower analysis error and greater cycling robustness than Gaussian ensemble benchmarks such as the LETKF, with improvements extending across spatial scales in the nonlinear SQG experiment. These results suggest that the principal benefit of CI-EnSF arises from combining nonlinear distributional transport with the mature covariance geometry used in conventional data assimilation.
tldr: The paper introduces a covariance-informed ensemble score filter (CI-EnSF) that embeds localized forecast-error covariance geometry into score-based diffusion transport for atmospheric data assimilation.
motivation: Standard ensemble and variational data assimilation methods rely on Gaussian or locally quadratic approximations, and existing ensemble score filters lack an intrinsic covariance-mediated pathway for propagating likelihood information from observed to unobserved state components.
method: The authors shape the forward diffusion by localized forecast-error covariance in a standardized state space, making it isotropic under a control-variable transformation, so that covariance structure propagates observational information throughout the reverse transport trajectory.
result: On Lorenz-96 and surface quasi-geostrophic dynamics, a well-tuned LETKF is more accurate for linear observations, while CI-EnSF achieves lower analysis error and greater cycling robustness under strongly nonlinear observations and climatological initialization.
conclusion: The main benefit of CI-EnSF comes from combining nonlinear distributional transport with conventional covariance geometry from data assimilation.

title: On The Limits Of Stochastic Push-Pull Over Time-Varying Digraphs
authors: Feiming Wang, Yutong He, Sulaiman Alghunaim, Kun Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic Push-Pull achieves linear speedup with respect to the network size [MATH] on static strongly connected digraphs, but whether this speedup persists on time-varying networks remains unclear. In this work, we construct a quadratic decentralized problem on period-two networks showing that stochastic Push-Pull may fail to attain linear speedup over time-varying digraphs. For [MATH]-periodic networks, we identify an effective node count [MATH] that governs the leading stochastic term. Specifically, for smooth nonconvex objectives, we establish convergence upper bounds and matching lower bounds for stochastic Push-Pull with constant stepsizes, both exhibiting the leading-order dependence [MATH]. When [MATH], the identity [MATH] recovers the usual linear speedup for static digraphs. However, periodic networks can have [MATH], demonstrating the loss of linear speedup under temporal variation. Numerical experiments illustrate effective-count scaling and the separation between static and periodic networks, consistent with our theoretical findings.
tldr: The paper shows that stochastic Push-Pull decentralized optimization loses linear speedup with respect to network size on time-varying (periodic) directed graphs, governed by an effective node count.
motivation: Stochastic Push-Pull provably achieves linear speedup on static strongly connected digraphs, but it was unclear whether this favorable scaling survives temporal network variation.
method: The authors construct a quadratic decentralized counterexample on period-two networks and derive convergence upper bounds and matching lower bounds for constant-stepsize stochastic Push-Pull on K-periodic digraphs, expressed in terms of an effective node count.
result: Both bounds exhibit leading-order dependence on the effective node count, which reduces to the standard network size for static graphs but can be much larger for periodic networks, implying loss of linear speedup.
conclusion: Temporal variation in directed network topology can fundamentally degrade the scaling of decentralized stochastic optimization, and the effective node count quantifies this degradation; numerical experiments support the theory.

title: Partial Rigidity And Q-additive Functions
authors: Trist\'an Radi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A system [MATH] is partially rigid with constant [MATH] if there exists an incresing sequence [MATH] such that [MATH] for every measurable [MATH]. The partial rigidity rate is the largest constant of partial rigidity. We characterize the partial rigidity rate of subshifts arising from [MATH]-additive functions [MATH] in terms of quantities arising from B\'esineau's theorem. With this, we build a family of strongly [MATH]-additive functions to deduce that the collection of partial rigidity rates for substitution subshifts is dense in [MATH] answering a question of Donoso, Maass and the author.
tldr: The paper characterizes the partial rigidity rate of subshifts generated by q-additive functions and shows that partial rigidity rates of substitution subshifts are dense in [0,1].
motivation: Partial rigidity is a quantitative measure of how close a measure-preserving system is to being rigid, and its rate was not understood for symbolic systems coming from q-additive functions; the authors also wanted to answer a question of Donoso, Maass and the author about which rates are attainable.
method: The partial rigidity rate of q-additive subshifts is expressed through quantities appearing in Bésineau's theorem, and a family of strongly q-additive functions is constructed to realize a dense set of rates for substitution subshifts.
result: An explicit formula for the partial rigidity rate of q-additive subshifts is obtained, and the set of partial rigidity rates of substitution subshifts is proven to be dense in [0,1].
conclusion: The work resolves the density question for substitution subshifts and connects Bésineau-type arithmetic quantities with ergodic-theoretic rigidity, purely within abstract ergodic theory and symbolic dynamics.

title: AgentTrace: Execution-Level Fingerprinting Of Black-Box Llm Agents
authors: Gejian Zhao, Hanzhou Wu, Xinpeng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Verifying the provenance of autonomous LLM agents is a critical security challenge. Existing semantic attribution is easily obfuscated by system prompts, while active watermarking conflicts with schema-constrained tool generation. We propose AgentTrace, an active framework that identifies the foundation model behind a black-box agent via observable execution traces. AgentTrace injects structurally ambiguous probes to trigger tokenization-sensitive serialization failures at rigid tool interfaces. While these initial failures provide coarse-grained separation across model families, the temporal sequence of subsequent repair operations reveals fine-grained, model-specific recovery behaviors. By modeling these multi-step trajectories with lightweight Markov chains, AgentTrace achieves 96.0% attribution accuracy under adversarial identity spoofing. Crucially, sequential repair modeling successfully distinguishes the evaluated intra-family variants sharing identical tokenizers (e.g., Llama-3 8B/70B), substantially outperforming unordered behavioral statistics while remaining robust against prompt obfuscation and temperature scaling.
tldr: AgentTrace is an active provenance-fingerprinting framework that identifies the foundation model behind a black-box LLM agent by analyzing the temporal sequence of tool-call repair operations triggered by deliberately crafted structural probes.
motivation: Semantic attribution of LLM agents is easily defeated by system-prompt obfuscation, and conventional watermarking interferes with schema-constrained tool generation, so a robust execution-level attribution mechanism is needed.
method: The framework injects structurally ambiguous probes that induce tokenization-sensitive serialization failures at rigid tool interfaces, then models the subsequent multi-step repair trajectories with lightweight Markov chains to extract model-specific behavioral signatures.
result: AgentTrace achieves 96.0% attribution accuracy under adversarial identity spoofing, distinguishes intra-family variants sharing identical tokenizers (e.g., Llama-3 8B/70B), and outperforms unordered behavioral statistics while remaining robust to prompt obfuscation and temperature scaling.
conclusion: Execution-trace fingerprinting via sequential repair dynamics offers a practical and robust route to LLM agent provenance verification, though the work lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: On The Propeller Conjecture
authors: Steven Heilman
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We simplify and improve OpenAI's proof of the propeller conjecture of Khot and Naor from 2008: the sum of the squared lengths of the Gaussian moments of any partition of Euclidean space is at most [MATH]. We show equality only occurs for three 120 degree sectors in the plane (up to symmetries, measure zero changes, and taking orthogonal cross products with Euclidean space). We also remove computer assistance from the three-dimensional case of the conjecture, which previously used an epsilon net traversal.
tldr: The paper simplifies and sharpens OpenAI's proof of the Khot–Naor propeller conjecture, showing that the sum of squared lengths of Gaussian moments over any partition of Euclidean space is bounded, with equality only for three 120-degree planar sectors (up to symmetries and orthogonal products).
motivation: The propeller conjecture of Khot and Naor (2008) is a geometric/analytic inequality about Gaussian moments of partitions of Euclidean space; the recent computer-assisted proof by OpenAI left room for simplification, generalization, and removal of numerical verification.
method: Analytical arguments that streamline the existing proof, extend the equality characterization to all dimensions, and replace the epsilon-net traversal in the three-dimensional case with a rigorous pen-and-paper argument.
result: A simpler proof of the conjecture is obtained, the equality case is fully classified (three 120-degree sectors times orthogonal Euclidean factors, up to measure-zero modifications), and the 3D case is made computer-free.
conclusion: The work settles and clarifies a purely mathematical Gaussian-moment inequality; it contains no quantum information, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-platform content.

title: On Task, Off Track: Benchmarking Llm And Agent Robustness To Near-Target Prompt Injection
authors: Yuyang Gong, Zihao Wang, Jiawei Liu, Xiaofeng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompt injection benchmarks assess whether large language models (LLMs) and agents resist malicious instructions embedded in external content. However, a system could perform well by rejecting attacks that obviously abandon the user's request, while still accepting changes that retain most of a legitimate answer but make it incorrect or harmful. Testing more instructions for unrelated outcomes would not necessarily reveal this weakness. We call attacks seeking responses designed to resemble legitimate answers while introducing incorrect or harmful changes near-target prompt injection. We introduce NTBench, the Near-Target Benchmark, which builds on legitimate tasks from existing datasets. For each task, a legitimate reference outcome guides the generation of target--instruction pairs, with separate tracks targeting incorrect and harmful outcomes in responses or agent tool invocations. Harmful targets can also accompany otherwise correct task completion. We combine LLM-based checks with human validation of the intended deviations, then assess whether injected instructions induce them using response judgments or tool-call checks, excluding deviations already observed without injection. We evaluate seven LLMs on ten datasets for language tasks and two agent benchmarks. Under a common budget of three attack executions per sample, both tracks achieve higher overall attack success rates than the fixed-target baseline for every evaluated model in each setting. On language tasks, the increases range from 9.3 to 35.8 percentage points for incorrect targets and 1.7 to 17.3 percentage points for harmful targets. These results show that resistance to the tested fixed-target attacks does not imply resistance to related incorrect or harmful outcomes, and that reference-guided targets broaden the failures revealed by robustness evaluation.
tldr: The paper introduces NTBench, a benchmark for near-target prompt injection that tests whether LLMs and agents accept subtly incorrect or harmful deviations resembling legitimate task outcomes.
motivation: Existing prompt-injection benchmarks may overestimate robustness because they test attacks that obviously abandon the user's request, missing attacks that preserve much of a valid answer while introducing targeted errors or harms.
method: NTBench builds on legitimate tasks from existing datasets, generates target-instruction pairs guided by reference outcomes, validates intended deviations with LLM-based checks and human review, and evaluates models via response judgments or tool-call checks while excluding baseline deviations.
result: Across seven LLMs, ten language datasets, and two agent benchmarks, near-target attacks under a three-execution budget achieve higher attack success rates than the fixed-target baseline, with increases of 9.3–35.8 percentage points for incorrect targets and 1.7–17.3 percentage points for harmful targets.
conclusion: Resistance to fixed-target prompt injection does not imply robustness to related incorrect or harmful outcomes, so reference-guided near-target targets broaden the failures revealed by robustness evaluation.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Loss Exploration For Vision-Based Perception Under Non-IID Data
authors: Nergiz Yuca, Christian Intern\`o, Nikolay Matyunin, Markus Olhofer, Barbara Hammer, Stefan Katzenbeisser
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-based image classification models benefit from Federated Learning (FL) across vehicles, however learning accurate models from distributed vehicular cameras is challenging due to data heterogeneity and privacy concerns. To improve performance on non-IID data, advanced FL optimization approaches have emerged that share auxiliary insights, such as client gradient behaviors. While these gradient-guided optimized FL methods improve the model accuracy, their reliance on sharing additional gradient information introduces a previously unexplored privacy vulnerability. In our empirical privacy-leakage experiment, we show that a malicious server can infer clients' label sets from shared guidance matrices under heterogeneous client label distributions (simulated via Dirichlet-based label partitions), between 50% and 84% accuracy. To address this privacy leakage, we propose PPFLex that replaces the central server with three Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) servers to securely compute the global guidance matrix and perform federated averaging under semi-honest and malicious MPC server assumptions. We evaluate PPFLex on widely used traffic-sign classification datasets (e.g., GTSRB and BTSC) as representative autonomous vehicle perception benchmarks, comparing against baselines. Our results show that PPFLex achieves accuracy comparable to the plain-text FedLEx pipeline while preventing privacy leakage, incurring acceptable MPC overhead.
tldr: The paper identifies a privacy leakage in gradient-guided federated learning for vision-based perception and proposes PPFLex, an MPC-based three-server protocol that computes guidance matrices and federated averaging without exposing client label information.
motivation: Federated learning across vehicular cameras suffers from non-IID data, and advanced gradient-sharing optimization methods that mitigate this improve accuracy but introduce an unexplored privacy vulnerability where a malicious server can infer client label sets.
method: The authors empirically demonstrate label-set inference attacks from shared guidance matrices under Dirichlet-based heterogeneous partitions, then replace the central server with three Secure Multi-Party Computation servers to securely compute the global guidance matrix and perform federated averaging under semi-honest and malicious assumptions.
result: The attack recovers clients' label sets with 50–84% accuracy; PPFLex achieves accuracy comparable to plaintext FedLEx on GTSRB and BTSC traffic-sign benchmarks while preventing the leakage at acceptable MPC overhead.
conclusion: Gradient-guided FL optimizations carry real privacy risks that can be mitigated with MPC-based server architectures without sacrificing model utility, though the work is purely classical machine-learning security.

title: AquaSense-ICS: A Hybrid Real-Simulated Cyber-Physical Dataset And Leakage-Aware Benchmark For Smart Water Quality Monitoring And Attack Detection
authors: Amal Neji, Mohamed Fourati, Lamia Chaari Fourati
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning research on water cyber-physical systems (CPS) is constrained by datasets that are either real but chemically poor, or simulated but free of sensing noise and attacks. We present AquaSense-ICS, an open dataset and benchmark that co-registers (i) a 25.4 h recording window (8.0 h of recorded data, 26% coverage) from a Raspberry Pi 5 edge node (TDS probe and BME680 ambient sensor, 1-2 s sampling, 23,688 records), with (ii) a looped network of 13 nodes (10 junctions, 2 reservoirs, 1 tank) simulated in EPANET-MSX for six water-quality species, (iii) a parameterised library of cyber-attacks (false data injection, replay, denial of service, drift) and unintentional sensor faults with sample-level ground truth, and (iv) augmented and TimeGAN-generated sequences, flagged by an origin column. The attack, fault and water-quality labels are traceable to a seeded generator, a documented rule or a simulation input. We show that the most common way of benchmarking such hybrid data, random row splits and labels computed from the input features, yields near-perfect but uninformative scores (macro-F1 = 0.9998 for Random Forest), and we replace it with a leakage-aware protocol using chronological splits and held-out attack types rather than label reconstruction. Under this protocol, no model exceeds the constant "normal" predictor for attack classification (macro-F1 = 0.465), and the best detectors reach a mean AUROC of 0.64 on attack types unseen during training (0.35-0.93 depending on the type), leaving substantial headroom. Data and simulation files are released under CC BY 4.0 at [URL] and attack generators and benchmark code under MIT.
tldr: AquaSense-ICS is a hybrid real-simulated cyber-physical dataset and leakage-aware benchmark for smart water quality monitoring and attack detection.
motivation: Machine-learning research on water cyber-physical systems is limited by datasets that are either real but chemically poor or simulated but lacking realistic sensing noise and attacks.
method: The authors combine Raspberry Pi sensor recordings with EPANET-MSX water-network simulations, a parameterized attack/fault library, and augmented/TimeGAN-generated sequences, then evaluate models under chronological and held-out-attack-type splits.
result: Under naive random splits, Random Forest reaches macro-F1 0.9998, but under leakage-aware evaluation no model exceeds the constant normal predictor for attack classification, with best mean AUROC 0.64 on unseen attack types.
conclusion: The dataset and benchmark expose serious leakage issues in hybrid CPS evaluation and provide a more realistic protocol, though the work is outside quantum information science.

title: Identity Amortization: Shared Resources And The Cost Of Sybil Attacks
authors: Homayoun Maleki, Nekane Sainz, Jon Legarda, Igor Santos-Grueiro
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sybil defenses commonly price identities by requiring a resource for each one. When one resource can support several identities, an adversary can pay less per identity than the defense intends. We call this identity amortization: a strict reduction in the minimum cost of provisioning identities when resources may be shared, relative to provisioning each one independently. It is a second route to the gap that a Sybil attack exploits. When influence is assigned per identity, a defense calibrated to the nominal price can overestimate the cost of a Sybil threshold by up to the number of identities one resource supports. For any resource catalogue, we give exact tests for when identity amortization occurs, where it begins, and its largest error; a sharing cap below the onset removes it. Because the tests need only prices and capacities, they apply to any defense that admits identities against a shareable resource, telling designers whether the assumed per-identity cost is paid, how wrong it can be, and which intervention restores it most cheaply for honest participants. On published phone-verification prices, per-account estimates overstate provisioning cost 1.6 to 4.3 times; Tor's raised per-address relay limit cut modeled attack cost by 8 to 72%, depending on the address-to-relay price ratio.
tldr: The paper introduces 'identity amortization', the phenomenon whereby adversaries in Sybil defenses can lower per-identity provisioning costs by sharing a single resource across multiple identities, and provides exact tests to detect and bound this effect.
motivation: Sybil defenses typically assume each identity costs one unit of a scarce resource, but when resources can be shared this pricing assumption breaks down, giving adversaries a cheaper route to mounting Sybil attacks than defenses anticipate.
method: Using only the price and capacity structure of a resource catalogue, the authors derive exact analytical tests characterizing when identity amortization occurs, where its onset lies, and the maximum overestimation error in attack-cost estimates; they also analyze sharing caps as a mitigation.
result: Applied to published phone-verification prices, per-account cost estimates overstate provisioning cost by 1.6–4.3x, and Tor's raised per-address relay limit cut modeled attack cost by 8–72% depending on the address-to-relay price ratio.
conclusion: Designers of Sybil defenses can use these price-and-capacity tests to check whether assumed per-identity costs are actually paid, quantify worst-case error, and choose the cheapest intervention that restores the intended cost structure for honest participants.

title: Choosing What To Observe: Higher-Order Obstructions In Horn Abduction
authors: Yukun Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An explanation may exist in every complete context yet be impossible to select from the information observed. We study this distinction in finite propositional Horn abduction with integrity constraints. Observations are sufficient when each report admits one hypothesis set that is consistent and entails the manifestation in every compatible context. We characterize sufficiency by minimal context families with no common explanation. Their variable spans form a canonical hypergraph whose transversals are exactly the sufficient observation sets. The characterization recovers classical discernibility for unique explanations and supports composition across independent components. Minimal obstructions have unbounded cardinality even for acyclic rules, while rectangular explanation families admit a tight bound given by their largest choice domain. With circuit-defined contexts, sufficiency is [MATH]-complete and selecting at most [MATH] observable variables is [MATH]-complete, already for unrestricted contexts and acyclic rules. The selection reduction makes observation choices enforce globally fixed existential commitments. Explicit contexts reduce both tasks to NP-complete problems; tabulated explanation families make sufficiency polynomial. These results connect explanatory choice, information requirements, and representation cost.
tldr: The paper characterizes when finite propositional Horn abduction observations suffice to single out an explanation, via hypergraph transversals of minimal context families, and analyzes the computational complexity of selecting observable variables.
motivation: In abductive reasoning an explanation may exist in every complete context yet be unselectable from partial observations; the authors want a precise theory of when an observation set is sufficient and how costly it is to choose one.
method: They define sufficiency for Horn abduction with integrity constraints, characterize it through minimal context families with no common explanation whose variable spans form a canonical hypergraph, and study circuit-defined contexts to obtain complexity results and reductions.
result: Sufficient observation sets are exactly the transversals of the canonical hypergraph; minimal obstructions can have unbounded cardinality even for acyclic rules, rectangular explanation families admit a tight bound, and sufficiency/selection are shown complete for high complexity classes, dropping to NP-complete for explicit contexts and polynomial for tabulated families.
conclusion: The work links explanatory choice, information requirements, and representation cost, providing a structural and complexity-theoretic account of observation selection in Horn abduction.

title: Logarithmic Separation Between Lz77 And LZ-End And Grammar Compression
authors: Philip Bille, Inge Li G{\o}rtz, Rikke Jessen, Jingxun Li, Simon Rumle Tarnow, Renfei Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there is a logarithmic separation between LZ77 and LZ-End, and between LZ77 and grammar compression.
tldr: The paper proves a logarithmic gap separating the compression power of LZ77 from that of LZ-End and from grammar-based compression.
motivation: LZ77, LZ-End, and grammar compression are widely used string compression schemes, but their relative compression power was not tightly characterized by known separations.
method: The authors construct string families and analyze parse sizes to derive asymptotic separation bounds between the LZ77 parse, LZ-End parse, and smallest grammar.
result: A logarithmic separation is shown between LZ77 and LZ-End, and likewise between LZ77 and grammar compression.
conclusion: LZ-End and grammar compression can be strictly, asymptotically stronger than LZ77, quantified by a logarithmic factor.

title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics Of Conway's Game Of Life In The Entropy--Complexity Plane
authors: Lucas Malacarne Astore, Alejandro C. Frery, Petr\^onio C\^andido de Lima E Silva, Frederico Gadelha Guimar\~aes
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31708v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the dynamics of Conway's Game of Life (GoL) through the lens of Ordinal Pattern analysis. Each GoL generation is transformed into a one-dimensional time series, from which ordinal patterns are extracted to characterize its underlying dynamics. The resulting ordinal distributions are then represented in the Entropy--Statistical Complexity ([MATH]) plane, enabling a quantitative analysis of the system's evolution. We evaluate different encoding strategies, including patch sizes and linearization methods, and assess their impact on the resulting [MATH] trajectories. Finally, we characterize the emergent dynamics in terms of convergence behavior, trajectory patterns, and statistical complexity, showing how the proposed entropy--complexity framework provides insights into the dynamics of cellular automata.
tldr: The paper analyzes Conway's Game of Life using ordinal-pattern statistics mapped onto an entropy–statistical-complexity plane.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize cellular-automaton dynamics quantitatively through information-theoretic complexity measures rather than only visual or phenomenological descriptions.
method: Each Game of Life generation is converted into a one-dimensional time series, ordinal patterns are extracted, and the resulting ordinal distributions are placed in the entropy–statistical-complexity plane; different patch sizes and linearization schemes are compared.
result: The approach yields trajectories in the entropy–complexity plane and reveals convergence behavior, trajectory patterns, and statistical-complexity signatures of the emergent dynamics.
conclusion: The entropy–complexity framework provides a useful quantitative lens on cellular-automaton dynamics, though the work is classical complex-systems analysis and not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spin Toda Systems And N-point Spherical Whittaker Functions
authors: Haoyi Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define and study a spin version of the open Toda integrable system, using the Iwasawa decomposition of a connected split real Lie group. We study spherical Whittaker functions as solutions of the spin Toda system. We also construct their N-point version and find the corresponding factorisation of the Casimir element, which yields asymptotic boundary KZB type equations.
tldr: The paper defines a spin version of the open Toda integrable system via the Iwasawa decomposition of a split real Lie group and studies spherical Whittaker functions as its solutions, including an N-point generalization and Casimir factorization yielding asymptotic boundary KZB-type equations.
motivation: Classical open Toda systems and spherical Whittaker functions are central objects in integrable systems and representation theory, and the authors aim to extend this structure to a 'spin' deformation with multi-point (N-point) generalizations.
method: The construction uses the Iwasawa decomposition of a connected split real Lie group to define the spin Toda system, then analyzes spherical Whittaker functions as solutions and derives an N-point version via a factorization of the Casimir element.
result: The authors obtain spherical Whittaker function solutions to the spin Toda system, construct their N-point counterparts, and show that the Casimir factorization produces asymptotic boundary Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov-Bernard (KZB) type equations.
conclusion: The work establishes a Lie-theoretic and representation-theoretic framework for spin Toda systems and connects them to conformal-field-theoretic KZB structures, though it lies entirely in pure mathematics.

title: Higher-order Asymptotic Formulae For Periodic Orbits Of 3-dimensional Volume-preserving Anosov Flows And The Foulon Conjecture
authors: Andrey Gogolev
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a volume-preserving Anosov flow of class [MATH] on a closed [MATH]-manifold. We consider a sequence of periodic orbits which shadow a homoclinic loop of a fixed periodic orbit [MATH], and derive higher-order asymptotic expansions for their periods [MATH] and for the logarithms of their unstable multipliers [MATH]. We give geometric interpretations of the coefficients in these expansions, in particular in terms of the Anosov cocycle (\`a la Hurder-Katok) and the longitudinal Anosov cocycle (\`a la Foulon-Hasselblatt), evaluated on [MATH]. Following the idea of De Simoi-Leguil-Vinhage-Yang, we compare these asymptotics when volume is the measure of maximal entropy. In this case, the equilibrium-state characterizations of volume and the measure of maximal entropy synchronize periods and exponents: [MATH]. Matching the coefficients of the two asymptotic expansions forces the cohomology classes of both cocycles to vanish. Then the work of Foulon-Hasselblatt on the longitudinal Anosov cocycle, together with Foulon's work on the contact case, yields the Foulon Conjecture for flows of class [MATH]: if volume is the measure of maximal entropy, then, up to a finite cover, [MATH] is smoothly conjugate either to a constant-roof suspension of a hyperbolic automorphism of the [MATH]-torus or to a finite cover of the constant-speed geodesic flow on a closed hyperbolic surface.
tldr: The paper derives higher-order asymptotic expansions for periods and unstable multipliers of periodic orbits shadowing homoclinic loops in 3D volume-preserving Anosov flows, and uses them to prove the Foulon Conjecture under a measure-of-maximal-entropy condition.
motivation: The Foulon Conjecture predicts strong rigidity for volume-preserving Anosov flows when volume is the measure of maximal entropy; the paper aims to establish this by comparing asymptotic invariants of periodic orbits.
method: The author computes higher-order asymptotic expansions for periods and logarithms of unstable multipliers along periodic orbits shadowing a homoclinic loop, interprets coefficients via Anosov cocycles, and compares expansions in the equilibrium-state setting where volume and the measure of maximal entropy synchronize.
result: Matching the asymptotic expansions forces the cohomology classes of the Anosov cocycle and longitudinal Anosov cocycle to vanish, which together with prior work of Foulon and Foulon-Hasselblatt yields the Foulon Conjecture for smooth volume-preserving Anosov flows on closed 3-manifolds.
conclusion: If volume is the measure of maximal entropy, then up to a finite cover the flow is smoothly conjugate either to a constant-roof suspension of a hyperbolic automorphism of the 3-torus or to a finite cover of the constant-speed geodesic flow on a closed hyperbolic surface.

title: Spectrum Of The Basilica Group And The Associated Real And Complex 2d Dynamics
authors: Eric Bedford, Rostislav Grigorchuk, Nguyen-Bac Dang, Mikhail Lyubich
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the iteration over the real and complex loci of a specific rational map, found by Grigorchuk and Zuk. This two dimensional map arises as the renormalization map which yields the density of states measure associated with the iterated monodromy group of the Basilica Julia set. It admits two natural complex currents, and we construct their real analogs and show that they are laminar. Finally, this yields some consequences on the properties of the density of states measures and its support.
tldr: The paper studies real and complex two-dimensional dynamics of a rational map associated with the Basilica group and its density of states measure.
motivation: The map arises as a renormalization map for the density of states measure associated with the iterated monodromy group of the Basilica Julia set, motivating a detailed dynamical study.
method: The authors analyze iteration on real and complex loci, construct real analogs of two natural complex currents, and prove laminarity properties.
result: They establish that the real currents are laminar and derive consequences for the density of states measures and their support.
conclusion: The work contributes to complex dynamics and group-related renormalization, with implications for density of states measures rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Strongly Non-linear Continuous Model For Wave Propagation In 2d Granular Media: Derivation And Hyperbolicity Analysis
authors: Sebastiano Cominelli, R\'egis Cottereau, Sergey Gavrilyuk, Bruno Lombard, Fabien Petitpas
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop a nonlinear continuum model for wave propagation in two-dimensional granular materials, building on key ideas from Nesterenko's work. Starting from the Hertzian contact law and neglecting contact friction, we derive an effective continuum description through homogenization, assuming spherical, monodisperse grains, local periodicity, and the Cauchy--Born hypothesis. The resulting strain-gradient model depends on both the first and second gradients of the displacement field. We analyse the hyperbolicity of the leading-order system through its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, establishing conditions for hyperbolicity within a restricted deformation domain. The model is solved using an explicit finite-volume method to investigate gravitational settling and wave propagation. We derive analytical expressions for the longitudinal and transverse wave speeds and highlight their dependence on depth. Finally, the predictions of the continuum model are compared with existing discrete-element simulations. This formulation allows several extensions, including more complex packing geometries, contact laws, and large-deformation regimes in which the contact network can evolve.
tldr: The authors derive a strain-gradient continuum model for nonlinear wave propagation in two-dimensional granular media and analyze its hyperbolicity and wave speeds.
motivation: Discrete-element simulations of granular packings are computationally expensive, so an effective continuum description building on Nesterenko's ideas is needed to capture nonlinear wave dynamics in granular materials.
method: Starting from the Hertzian contact law without friction, they homogenize spherical monodisperse locally periodic packings under the Cauchy-Born hypothesis, obtaining a strain-gradient model whose leading-order hyperbolicity is studied via eigenvalues and eigenvectors and which is solved with an explicit finite-volume scheme.
result: Hyperbolicity holds only within a restricted deformation domain; analytical expressions for depth-dependent longitudinal and transverse wave speeds are derived and compared with discrete-element simulations for gravitational settling and wave propagation.
conclusion: The continuum formulation reproduces discrete-element behavior and admits extensions to more complex packings, contact laws, and large-deformation regimes with evolving contact networks.

title: CoPiT: A Conditional Position-induced Transformer For Aerodynamic Field Prediction On Unstructured Meshes
authors: Junfeng Chen, Yongchen Fan, Zhonghua Qiao, Kailiang Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) simulations remain a standard tool for aerodynamic analysis, yet each solve on an unstructured mesh is computationally expensive, making many-query tasks such as design exploration, optimization, and multi-condition evaluation costly. Neural operators provide mesh-flexible surrogates for mapping geometry and operating conditions to flow fields; however, in many existing architectures, global parameters such as the freestream state and design variables are concatenated with pointwise inputs, leaving their influence on intermediate features implicit. This paper proposes CoPiT, a nditional osition-induced ransformer that builds on the Position-induced Transformer (PiT) as its geometric backbone and injects a global condition vector through multi-stage feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), thereby making parametric modulation explicit while preserving geometry-based attention weights. The model is evaluated on two-dimensional AirfRANS airfoil fields, including scarce-data and extrapolation regimes, and on three-dimensional BlendedNet++ blended-wing-body surfaces. On the AirfRANS full-data test set, CoPiT reduces surface and volume losses by approximately 54\% and 24\% relative to Transolver, respectively, and achieves the lowest overall normalized test MSE among the compared baselines on BlendedNet++. Matched ablations show that FiLM conditioning generally improves upon input concatenation, while the preferred placement is task-dependent. CoPiT thus provides a practical operator-learning surrogate for parametric aerodynamics on unstructured meshes.
tldr: CoPiT is a conditional position-induced transformer that predicts aerodynamic flow fields on unstructured meshes by injecting global freestream/design conditions via multi-stage FiLM modulation.
motivation: High-fidelity RANS simulations are too costly for many-query design tasks, and existing neural-operator surrogates treat global parameters implicitly by simple input concatenation, weakening their influence on intermediate features.
method: The authors build on the Position-induced Transformer as a geometric backbone and add feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) stages driven by a global condition vector, keeping geometry-based attention weights intact; evaluated on 2D AirfRANS and 3D BlendedNet++.
result: On AirfRANS full-data, CoPiT cuts surface and volume losses by ~54% and ~24% versus Transolver, and attains the best normalized test MSE on BlendedNet++; ablations show FiLM generally beats input concatenation with task-dependent placement.
conclusion: FiLM-based explicit conditioning yields a practical, mesh-flexible operator-learning surrogate for parametric aerodynamic prediction, though the work lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: A Globally Convergent Newton Method For Nonsmooth Optimization In The Absence Of Smooth Surrogates
authors: Tran T. A. Nghia, Nghia V. Vo, Khoa V. H. Vu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a globally convergent Newton method for convex composite optimization problems with polyhedral regularizers. The method rests on the observation that the proximal gradient step yields not only a new point but also a subgradient, which determines the face on which the linearization of the regularizer is exact. Minimizing a second-order model of the objective over this face produces a Newton direction that involves no generalized second-order information about the regularizer and is a descent direction for the objective itself. The method is therefore globalized by an Armijo line search on the original objective which, unlike forward-backward envelope techniques, requires only evaluations of the smooth component. We establish global convergence and local quadratic convergence to tilt-stable minimizers without any nondegeneracy condition, and show that the unit step is always accepted when the smooth component is quadratic, which yields a line-search-free method. The subproblems require only projections onto faces, which are explicit for the Lasso and nonnegative least squares and computable in linear time for the fused Lasso. Numerical experiments show that the method compares favorably with state-of-the-art solvers.
tldr: The paper introduces a globally convergent Newton-type method for convex composite optimization with polyhedral regularizers, avoiding generalized second-order information about the regularizer.
motivation: Nonsmooth convex composite problems with polyhedral regularizers (e.g., Lasso, fused Lasso) lack smooth surrogates, making classical Newton methods inapplicable and motivating a new approach that exploits the structure revealed by proximal gradient steps.
method: A proximal gradient step yields a subgradient identifying the face where the regularizer's linearization is exact; a second-order model of the objective is minimized over that face to obtain a Newton direction, globalized by an Armijo line search on the original objective requiring only smooth-component evaluations.
result: The authors prove global convergence and local quadratic convergence to tilt-stable minimizers without nondegeneracy assumptions, show the unit step is always accepted for quadratic smooth components (giving a line-search-free method), and demonstrate favorable numerical performance against state-of-the-art solvers.
conclusion: The method provides a practical, globally convergent Newton scheme for polyhedral-regularized composite optimization with explicit projection-based subproblems and strong local convergence guarantees.

title: Optimal Convergence Of Quadratic Not-a-Knot Spline Interpolation On Arbitrary Partitions
authors: Aussie Greene
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The not-a-knot condition provides a simple spline interpolation scheme that requires no derivative data at the endpoints. Whereas the classical not-a-knot scheme using odd-degree splines selects knots that coincide with the data points, this approach does not extend to the even-degree case. In this paper we establish the well-posedness of the not-a-knot interpolation problem for even-degree splines, where knots are selected at midpoints of data values. We then show that the quadratic case, introduced in [M. J. D. Powell, Approximation Theory and Methods, Cambridge University Press, 1981], achieves [MATH] convergence for [MATH] functions on arbitrary partitions without mesh-ratio restrictions. The proof derives a linear system defining the interpolating spline, normalizes the system to bound the matrix norm of its inverse using a Neumann-series argument, and establishes global error bounds.
tldr: This paper establishes well-posedness and optimal O(h^3) convergence of quadratic not-a-knot spline interpolation for C^2 functions on arbitrary partitions without mesh-ratio restrictions.
motivation: The classical not-a-knot spline scheme relies on odd-degree splines with knots coinciding with data points, an approach that fails to extend to even degrees; the authors seek a well-defined even-degree analogue.
method: Knots are placed at midpoints of data values; the interpolating spline is characterized via a linear system, which is normalized and bounded through a Neumann-series argument to control the inverse matrix norm, yielding global error bounds.
result: The quadratic not-a-knot interpolation problem is shown to be well-posed and to achieve cubic-order convergence for C^2 functions on arbitrary partitions, with no mesh-ratio constraints.
conclusion: The midpoint-knot even-degree not-a-knot scheme provides a robust, mesh-ratio-free alternative to classical odd-degree not-a-knot interpolation, with rigorously proven optimal convergence.

title: Continuous-Time Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Control: Limits, Duality, And Stability
authors: Minjung Gim, Hee Jun Yang, Yeoneung Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A sampled robust control problem averages future values over disturbance laws, while its continuous-time counterpart evolves with an averaged drift. We establish a fluid limit connecting these two models for Wasserstein ambiguity sets. Under a uniform disturbance moment bound and subcritical growth, sampled Bellman values converge locally uniformly to the upper and lower values of a discounted differential game. The argument accommodates unbounded disturbances without requiring square-integrable increments. We also derive an explicit bound on the change in either game value when both the radius and center of the ambiguity set vary. For Euclidean disturbance space, uniform Lipschitz continuity in the disturbance, common state and cost Lipschitz bounds, and a discount rate exceeding the drift's state Lipschitz constant, this estimate converts distributional confidence bounds into uniform value approximation bounds. Static Wasserstein duality reformulates pointwise distributional optimization; affine disturbance dependence permits an exact reduction to a ball of means. Experiments illustrate the common limit and decreasing value error with sample size. For a nonlinear disturbance model, uniform shifts overestimate worst-case recovery speed by about 36\%. In a two-product inventory model, increasing ambiguity raises production near balance while reducing the region of full production in deeper backlogs.
tldr: The paper establishes a fluid limit connecting discrete-time sampled Wasserstein distributionally robust control with a continuous-time differential game, deriving explicit value-perturbation bounds and duality reductions.
motivation: Sampled robust control and its continuous-time averaged-drift counterpart are used in practice but the relationship between them, and the stability of the resulting values under ambiguity-set perturbation, were not rigorously established.
method: Under uniform disturbance moment bounds and subcritical growth, the authors prove local uniform convergence of sampled Bellman values to the upper and lower values of a discounted differential game, and use static Wasserstein duality plus affine disturbance dependence to reduce the distributional optimization to a ball of means.
result: They obtain an explicit bound on value change under simultaneous radius/center variation, which under Lipschitz and discount-rate conditions converts distributional confidence bounds into uniform value approximation bounds; experiments confirm the common limit and roughly 36% overestimation of worst-case recovery speed under a nonlinear disturbance model.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous bridge between sampled and continuous-time distributionally robust control and quantifies sensitivity to ambiguity-set choice, with applications such as inventory control.

title: Timed Recovery Safe Gradient Flows For Constrained Nonlinear Programming
authors: Tianxi Luo, Yue Wu, Fei Chen, Hongsheng Qi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies how to relax pointwise feasibility in continuous-time dynamics for inequality-constrained nonlinear programming while retaining a quantitative feasible-recovery guarantee. Existing safe gradient flows enforce forward invariance of the feasible set, which yields an anytime-feasible dynamics but can be overly restrictive for optimization because it suppresses transient infeasible motion that may be essential for effective descent. To address this limitation, we propose a timed recovery safe gradient flow that replaces pointwise feasibility with fixed-horizon feasible recovery. The proposed construction augments the state with a timer that records the elapsed infeasible duration and computes a minimum-norm correction to the nominal gradient flow through a pointwise convex quadratic program. We show that the resulting augmented safe set is forward invariant and that every trajectory initialized from the feasible set returns to it within every time window of length \(\tau\). We further show that, in a strict interior inactive regime, the closed-loop dynamics reduces exactly to the nominal gradient flow and recovers the corresponding local convergence behavior. Numerical examples illustrate how the recovery horizon shapes the closed-loop behavior and corroborate the theoretical analysis.
tldr: The paper proposes a timed recovery safe gradient flow for inequality-constrained nonlinear programming that replaces pointwise feasibility with fixed-horizon feasible recovery.
motivation: Existing safe gradient flows enforce forward invariance of the feasible set, which can be overly restrictive because transient infeasible motion may be necessary for effective descent.
method: The authors augment the state with a timer recording elapsed infeasible duration and compute a minimum-norm correction to the nominal gradient flow via a pointwise convex quadratic program.
result: They prove forward invariance of the augmented safe set and show that trajectories initialized in the feasible set return to it within every time window of length tau; in a strict interior inactive regime the dynamics reduce to the nominal gradient flow.
conclusion: Numerical examples illustrate how the recovery horizon shapes closed-loop behavior and support the theoretical guarantees.

title: Weak Adversarial Tensor Neural Network For High-dimensional Fokker-Planck Equations
authors: Zhongwei Xu Sihong Shao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solving high-dimensional stationary Fokker-Planck (SFP) equations remains challenging. Recently, deep learning methods have shown great potential for solving high-dimensional SFP equations due to their universal approximation and mesh-free training. However, the high-dimensional integrals involved in loss computation and normalization can be expensive to approximate accurately using Monte Carlo integration. To address this issue, we propose a weak adversarial tensor neural network (WATNN) method for solving high-dimensional SFP equations, which combines a weak adversarial (WA) formulation with the tensor neural network (TNN). The WA formulation avoids the cross terms introduced by squaring the strong residual, reducing the number of integrals to be computed. When both the primal network and the adversarial test network are set as TNNs, the TNN quadrature scheme provides accurate and efficient normalization and loss computation with relatively few fixed quadrature points, avoiding the statistical sampling error that arises when using Monte Carlo integration. We demonstrate the effectiveness numerically on four high-dimensional SFP equations. For the 6D unimodal, 6D multi-modal, 10D multi-modal and 20D multi-modal problems, WATNN achieves the mean relative errors of 1.50%, 1.13%, 1.20% and 7.93% respectively, in only a few minutes.
tldr: The authors propose a weak adversarial tensor neural network (WATNN) method to solve high-dimensional stationary Fokker-Planck equations efficiently without Monte Carlo sampling error.
motivation: Deep learning solvers for high-dimensional stationary Fokker-Planck equations suffer from expensive and inaccurate Monte Carlo estimation of the high-dimensional integrals in the loss and normalization terms.
method: A weak adversarial formulation is combined with tensor neural networks (TNNs) for both the primal solution and the adversarial test function, so that cross terms from squaring the strong residual are avoided and TNN quadrature provides accurate, cheap normalization and loss evaluation at fixed quadrature points.
result: On four high-dimensional SFP benchmarks (6D unimodal, 6D, 10D and 20D multimodal) WATNN attains mean relative errors of 1.50%, 1.13%, 1.20% and 7.93% within minutes.
conclusion: WATNN offers an accurate and efficient mesh-free approach to high-dimensional Fokker-Planck equations, though it is a classical numerical/ML contribution with no quantum information component.

title: An Energy-stable Parametric Finite Element Framework For Surface Diffusion With Moving Contact Lines On Curved Substrates
authors: Harald Garcke, Robert N\"urnberg, Rong Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop energy-stable parametric finite element methods for surface diffusion of solid films with moving contact lines on curved substrates. Discretizing both the film surface and the substrate patches allows the introduction of linear schemes that are unconditionally energy stable. A nonlinear variant of the schemes ensures that, in addition, the vertices of the substrate approximations remain attached to the true substrate throughout. Moreover, our framework can incorporate anisotropic surface energy densities, for both the film surface and the substrate, as well as different tangential motions. Numerical experiments in two and three space dimensions illustrate the practicality of the introduced methods.
tldr: The paper develops energy-stable parametric finite element schemes for surface diffusion of thin solid films with moving contact lines on curved substrates.
motivation: Simulating surface diffusion with moving contact lines on curved substrates requires discretizations that preserve the geometric constraint of the contact line and remain stable, which is difficult for existing numerical methods.
method: Parametric finite element discretizations of both the film surface and substrate patches yield linear, unconditionally energy-stable schemes, plus a nonlinear variant that keeps substrate vertices attached to the true substrate; anisotropic surface energies and tangential motions are incorporated.
result: Numerical experiments in two and three space dimensions demonstrate the practicality and stability of the proposed schemes, including anisotropic and tangential-motion cases.
conclusion: The framework provides a robust, energy-stable numerical tool for surface diffusion problems with moving contact lines on curved geometries.

title: Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection Reinforcement Learning Problems For A Markov Regime-Switching System With No-Shorting Constraints
authors: Minghui Zhang, Xun Li, Xin Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is the first to study the continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem with no-shorting constraints in a Markov regime-switching market using reinforcement learning (RL). The main challenge stems from the interaction between random regime shifts and portfolio non-negativity constraints, which typically causes the coupled Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations to lose smoothness across different state regions. Additionally, directly imposing no-shorting constraints on randomized policies disrupts their analytically tractable Gaussian structure, complicating both exploratory modeling and reinforcement learning. To address these challenges, we propose an auxiliary exploratory approach that limits the policy to a Gaussian distribution and applies the no-shorting constraint solely to its mean. We explicitly characterize the optimal policy for this auxiliary problem and demonstrate that, by appropriately selecting the exploration variance, its optimal mean policy exactly matches the optimal policy of the original constrained mean-variance problem. Building upon this analytical framework, we develop a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the optimal portfolio policy directly from trajectory data. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results and show that the proposed method can effectively recover the optimal no-shorting portfolio in a regime-switching market.
tldr: Develops a model-free reinforcement learning method for continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection with no-shorting constraints in a Markov regime-switching market.
motivation: Regime shifts combined with portfolio non-negativity constraints break HJB smoothness and destroy the Gaussian tractability of randomized policies, making existing RL approaches for mean-variance problems inapplicable.
method: Introduces an auxiliary exploratory problem restricting policies to Gaussians and applying no-shorting only to the mean, characterizes its optimal solution analytically, and proves an appropriate choice of exploration variance makes the auxiliary optimal mean coincide with the original constrained optimum; then builds a model-free RL algorithm trained on trajectory data.
result: Theoretical equivalence between the auxiliary and original constrained problems is established, and numerical experiments recover the optimal no-shorting portfolio under regime switching.
conclusion: The auxiliary-exploration framework enables principled model-free RL for constrained continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection in regime-switching markets.

title: Long-time Stability And Convergence Of A Bdf3 Method For A Parabolic Equation With Fading Memory
authors: Wenlin Qiu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the long-time stability and convergence of a third-order backward differentiation formula (BDF3) for parabolic equations with exponentially fading memory. The BDF3 scalar resolvent has oscillatory coefficients, so the monotonicity argument used for lower-order formulas in [Math. Comp. 62 (1994) 477-496] does not apply. We instead control memory feedback by the absolute mass of its discrete Green sequence and establish the rigorous stability-constant bounds [MATH]. A causal third-order memory quadrature with nonnegative assembled weights then yields exponentially weighted stability without a parabolic step-size restriction. With third-order starting values, we prove a uniform-in-time third-order temporal error estimate and extend it to conforming finite elements. Numerical tests confirm the predicted convergence orders and the long-time behavior.
tldr: The paper analyzes long-time stability and third-order convergence of a BDF3 scheme for parabolic equations with exponentially fading memory.
motivation: Higher-order BDF methods for memory-containing parabolic problems are difficult to analyze because BDF3 has oscillatory resolvent coefficients, so existing monotonicity arguments do not apply.
method: The authors control memory feedback using the absolute mass of the discrete Green sequence, establish stability-constant bounds, and combine a causal third-order memory quadrature with nonnegative assembled weights.
result: They prove uniform-in-time third-order temporal error estimates, extend the analysis to conforming finite elements, and confirm the convergence orders numerically.
conclusion: The proposed approach removes parabolic step-size restrictions and provides rigorous long-time stability and convergence for BDF3 discretizations of fading-memory parabolic equations.

title: On The Homeomorphism Group Of The Cantor Set: Monotone And Measure Preserving Maps
authors: Benjamin Vejnar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be the Cantor set, [MATH], let [MATH] be the group of order preserving homeomorphisms and [MATH] the group of homeomorphisms preserving the Cantor--Lebesgue measure [MATH]. We study how [MATH] is built from these two subgroups. In 2003, Glasner and Weiss stated that [MATH]. We show that this is not the case, in fact [MATH] and [MATH] are two different proper subsets of [MATH]. On the other hand, [MATH] is a dense [MATH] subset of [MATH], the multiplication map [MATH] is a homeomorphism, and [MATH]. In particular, every homeomorphism of [MATH] is conjugate to an element of [MATH]. We classify the double cosets [MATH] using special clopen values set. There are continuum many of them, and [MATH] is the only one which is not meager. We prove that [MATH] is topologically generated by one element of [MATH] and one element of [MATH] and these two generators produce the Thompson's group [MATH]. We also show that the generic homeomorphism of [MATH] is the product of a generic element of [MATH] and a generic element of [MATH]. The equality [MATH] fails also if [MATH] is replaced by any other full nonatomic measure.
tldr: A pure topological group theory paper analyzing how the homeomorphism group of the Cantor set decomposes into order-preserving and measure-preserving subgroups, correcting a 2003 claim of Glasner and Weiss.
motivation: Glasner and Weiss asserted in 2003 that the full homeomorphism group of the Cantor set equals the product of the order-preserving and measure-preserving subgroups; the author aims to test and correct this structural claim.
method: Descriptive set theory and topological group techniques: double-coset classification via special clopen value sets, Baire category (meagerness) arguments, and topological generation results linked to Thompson's group.
result: The claimed equality fails; the two subgroups are proper subsets, their product set is dense but meager-complemented, the multiplication map is a homeomorphism on the relevant domain, every homeomorphism is conjugate into the measure-preserving subgroup, and there are continuum many double cosets with only one non-meager.
conclusion: The algebraic and topological structure of Homeo(Cantor set) is shown to be strictly richer than previously stated, with genericity and conjugacy results tying it to Thompson's group V.

title: Sempre: Semantic-Aware Protocol Reverse Engineering Via Consistency-Driven Joint Optimization
authors: Yihua Xu, Weijie Huang, Xiaofeng Wang, Hang Zhang, Binghui Wang, Yue Duan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protocol reverse engineering (PRE) is essential for understanding undocumented or proprietary communication formats, enabling security-critical tasks such as vulnerability discovery, malware C2 analysis, and IDS signature generation. However, existing PRE techniques rely on brittle hand-written rules, under-model contextual dependencies among neighboring fields, and often fail on messages with nested sub-protocols. We present SEMPRE, a fully automated PRE framework that replaces ad-hoc heuristics with recursive LLM reasoning grounded in fine-grained dynamic program analysis. SEMPRE uses taint-flow and loop traces to guide an LLM-driven tree-of-thought search that slices messages into fields while detecting nested sub-payloads, producing a hierarchical layout. It then infers each field's type and role and iteratively refines boundaries by freezing high-confidence segments and re-running detection under semantic constraints, yielding an EM-style procedure that monotonically improves structure and semantics until convergence. Evaluated on a broad corpus of mainstream protocols against six state-of-the-art (vs. <0.4 for all baselines) and 0.72 for semantic inference (vs. 0.13 for BinPRE).
