Ablations confirm the contribution of each component, and a case study on a prolific real-world botnet demonstrates practical utility.
tldr: SEMPRE is a fully automated protocol reverse engineering framework that couples taint-flow/loop-trace dynamic analysis with LLM-driven tree-of-thought reasoning to recover hierarchical message formats and field semantics.
motivation: Existing protocol reverse engineering tools depend on brittle hand-written heuristics, ignore contextual dependencies between neighboring fields, and break down on messages containing nested sub-protocols.
method: The system uses dynamic taint-flow and loop traces to steer an LLM tree-of-thought search that slices messages into fields, detects nested sub-payloads, infers field types and roles, and then iteratively refines boundaries in an EM-style freezing/re-detection loop until convergence.
result: On a broad corpus of mainstream protocols it substantially outperforms six state-of-the-art baselines (baselines all below 0.4 on the main metric) and reaches 0.72 semantic inference accuracy versus 0.13 for BinPRE, with ablations and a real-world botnet case study confirming each component's value.
conclusion: LLM reasoning grounded in fine-grained program analysis offers a practical, fully automated route to accurate hierarchical protocol inference for security applications such as vulnerability discovery and malware C2 analysis.

title: Agentic Ai Defense: Decode-Time Provenance Binding For Mcp
authors: Eric Yocam, Varghese Vaidyan, Paris Kalathas, Patrick Tague, Bruce Debruhl, Yong Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic AI systems using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection through untrusted tool outputs. We demonstrate cross-modal trust laundering, in which instructions concealed in an email-signature image using least-significant-bit (LSB), discrete cosine transform (DCT), or metadata steganography bypass text scanners and enter a multi-agent workflow when decoded by a tool. To counter this threat, we propose decode-time provenance binding, which combines HMAC-authenticated trust labels with an MCP-maintained provenance ledger and context-taint tracking. The mechanism labels decoded content as untrusted and blocks critical tool calls influenced by that content, even when a compromised agent substitutes a valid trusted label. We evaluate the approach using a real MCP testbed with three steganographic carriers and 24 adaptive payloads. The undefended pipeline exhibits 100% attack success, while keyword and regex defenses each permit 62.5% of attacks. Our mechanism blocks all attacks (0% success), including adversarial label substitution across mediated agent boundaries. A four-component ablation validates the roles of decode marking, cryptographic authentication, lineage tracking, and sink enforcement. An audited trusted-promotion mechanism increases legitimate-task completion from 67% to 100% without compromising protection. The approach provides carrier-independent containment within fully mediated MCP execution environments. Code and data are publicly available.
tldr: The paper proposes decode-time provenance binding, an HMAC-based provenance and taint-tracking defense against indirect prompt injection via steganographic content in agentic AI workflows using the Model Context Protocol.
motivation: Agentic AI systems that consume untrusted tool outputs via MCP can be attacked by instructions hidden in images or metadata that bypass text scanners once decoded, enabling cross-modal trust laundering.
method: The authors combine HMAC-authenticated trust labels, an MCP-maintained provenance ledger, and context-taint tracking to mark decoded content as untrusted and block critical tool calls influenced by it, tested on a real MCP testbed with three steganographic carriers and 24 adaptive payloads plus a four-component ablation.
result: Undefended pipelines show 100% attack success and keyword/regex defenses allow 62.5%, while the proposed mechanism blocks all attacks (0% success) including adversarial label substitution, and an audited trusted-promotion mechanism raises legitimate task completion from 67% to 100%.
conclusion: Decode-time provenance binding provides carrier-independent containment of indirect prompt injection in fully mediated MCP execution environments, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Spa: Structure-Preserving Approximation Of Gated Activations Under Fhe
authors: Rui Li, Wenyuan Wu, Weijie Miao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear activation evaluation remains a major bottleneck in neural inference under fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). FHE supports efficient addition and multiplication, but lacks native operations for exponential functions, reciprocals, and value-dependent selection. High-degree polynomial approximations on fixed intervals are therefore commonly used to replace nonlinear activations. They can achieve small errors but often incur substantial multiplicative depth and latency. We observe that several widely used nonlinear activations share the algebraic structure [MATH] with [MATH]. This class includes GELU, SiLU, fixed-parameter Swish, and the scalar nonlinear branches of GEGLU/SwiGLU. We propose \SPA{} () to exploit this shared structure. \SPA{} retains the exact odd component [MATH] and approximates only the even residual as a polynomial in [MATH], yielding a comparison-free arithmetic kernel. This construction removes redundant odd degrees of freedom and enables lower-cost polynomial evaluation at a given error target. Plaintext experiments with Gemma-4-E2B and Llama-3.2-3B show that SPA largely preserves downstream task performance without weight updates. Fixed-interval CKKS benchmarks show favorable error--latency trade-offs. On [MATH], \SPA{}-balanced achieves a [MATH] speedup over MOAI (ICLR'~26) for erf-GELU with comparable error. On the same interval, \SPA{}-accurate achieves [MATH] lower root mean squared error (RMSE) and a [MATH] speedup over Euston (S\&P'~26) for QuickGELU. For SiLU, \SPA{}-accurate achieves [MATH] lower RMSE and a [MATH] speedup over THOR (CCS'~25).
tldr: SPA exploits the shared algebraic structure of gated activations (GELU, SiLU, Swish, GEGLU/SwiGLU) to build cheaper comparison-free polynomial approximations for neural inference under fully homomorphic encryption.
motivation: Nonlinear activation evaluation is the main bottleneck in FHE-based neural inference because FHE natively supports only addition and multiplication, so high-degree polynomial approximations are needed but incur large multiplicative depth and latency.
method: The authors keep the exact odd component of the activation and approximate only the even residual as a polynomial in the squared argument, removing redundant odd degrees of freedom and yielding a lower-cost arithmetic kernel evaluated in CKKS.
result: Plaintext experiments with Gemma-4-E2B and Llama-3.2-3B preserve downstream performance without weight updates; CKKS benchmarks show speedups over MOAI, Euston, and THOR with comparable or lower RMSE.
conclusion: Structure-preserving approximation gives favorable error-latency trade-offs for encrypted inference, though the work is a classical cryptographic/ML engineering contribution.

title: Detecting Insecure Compositions Of Clean Agent Skills Via Capability-Flow Graph Analysis
authors: Yihao Li, Chuanpu Fu, Yizhou Zhao, Miao Chen, Qi Li, Ke Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents increasingly extend their capabilities by invoking third-party skills, where each skill encapsulates instructions, scripts, and resources for agents to execute on demand. This paper reveals that deploying many benign skills together introduces compositional security risks: multiple individually clean skills can compose into safety-violation chains, because the agent passes an upstream skill's output to a downstream skill's input across invocations. The risk arises not from any single skill, but from the agent's runtime orchestration, and thus cannot be captured by existing malicious skill detection methods. To this end, we develop KnotScryer to detect insecure skill compositions by treating skills as typed capability flows. In particular, we abstract each skill into a capability summary, and construct the Skill Capability-Flow Graph (SCFG), where edges denote cross-skill information flow. Moreover, we design a search policy that tracks protected or untrusted data along handoff edges to locate paths reaching insecure operations. Finally, a two-layer verification method replays the insecure information flow for reachability analysis and applies a task-anchored LLM chain audit to confirm the semantic plausibility of the identified violation chains. We deploy KnotScryer to analyze 13,598 clean skills from ClawHub, and validate the detected chains across three agent frameworks and three LLMs. KnotScryer identifies 612 insecure compositions, which are consistently exploited across agent frameworks. Meanwhile, under GLM-5.1, it outperforms tag-match and graph-only baselines by improving the exploitation rate from 16.5%-18.2% to 85.6%, while reducing the search space by 85.3%. Furthermore, 13.7% of the detected chains consist entirely of skills labeled safe by a single-skill scanner, showing that KnotScryer effectively identifies insecure compositions that per-skill auditing cannot.
tldr: KnotScryer detects insecure compositions of individually benign AI-agent skills by modeling them as typed capability flows in a Skill Capability-Flow Graph and auditing violation chains with reachability analysis plus task-anchored LLM chain auditing.
motivation: AI agents increasingly orchestrate third-party skills, and multiple individually clean skills can chain into safety-violating information flows through runtime handoffs, a compositional risk invisible to per-skill malicious-skill scanners.
method: Each skill is abstracted into a capability summary; cross-skill information flows form the SCFG, over which a tracking search policy follows protected or untrusted data along handoff edges, followed by two-layer verification (replay-based reachability analysis and task-anchored LLM chain audit).
result: Applied to 13,598 clean skills from ClawHub across three agent frameworks and three LLMs, KnotScryer found 612 insecure compositions, raising the exploitation rate from 16.5%-18.2% (baselines) to 85.6% under GLM-5.1 while cutting search space 85.3%; 13.7% of chains used only skills flagged safe by single-skill scanners.
conclusion: Compositional security auditing of agent skill ecosystems is both necessary and feasible, and capability-flow graph analysis exposes violation chains that per-skill auditing fundamentally cannot detect.

title: Data-Efficient Backdoor Attacks On Code Models Via Trigger-Neutralized Counterfactual Scoring
authors: Yu-Yu Lee, Ming-Feng Tsai, Tomohiro Morikawa, Chun-I Fan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pre-trained code models are exposed to backdoor poisoning, in which crafted training samples make the model misbehave on a trigger. A capable attacker minimizes the number of such samples, since each adds cost and exposure and a lower poisoning rate leaves a smaller footprint for defenses. Which samples to poison therefore matters, but existing data-efficient selection methods target image classification, offer no scoring mechanism for autoregressive generation, and have not been studied on code. We propose Trigger-Neutralized Counterfactual Scoring (TNCS), which isolates a trigger's contribution to the target behavior by comparing the scoring model's output on a triggered input with its output on a trigger-neutralized counterfactual, covering classification and generation alike. TNCS attains higher attack success rates than the baselines at very low poisoning ratios, across three CodeXGLUE tasks and five trigger families, without degrading clean-task performance, and its margin grows as the ratio decreases. It is the only method effective on every trigger family, and its selected poison set transfers to mismatched victims.
tldr: The paper proposes Trigger-Neutralized Counterfactual Scoring (TNCS), a data-efficient poison-sample selection method for backdoor attacks against pre-trained code models.
motivation: Attackers want to minimize the number of poisoned training samples to reduce cost and detectability, but existing data-efficient selection methods were designed for image classification and do not handle autoregressive code generation.
method: TNCS scores candidate poisoning samples by comparing a model's output on a triggered input against a trigger-neutralized counterfactual, thereby isolating the trigger's causal contribution to the target behavior for both classification and generation tasks.
result: Across three CodeXGLUE tasks and five trigger families, TNCS achieves higher attack success rates than baselines at very low poisoning ratios, is the only method effective on every trigger family, preserves clean-task performance, and its poison sets transfer to mismatched victim models.
conclusion: Counterfactual trigger attribution provides a practical, data-efficient route to backdoor poisoning of code models, with implications for both red-teaming and defense design.

title: Developing Security Metrics For Automated Compliance Checking
authors: Immanuel Kunz, Nico Haas, Angelika Schneider, Christian Banse
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To automatically check for compliance with security-related standards, prose requirements must be translated to technical properties to make them measurable. A multitude of metrics have been proposed in past literature, but they are lacking a systematic methodology for their elicitation. Without such a methodology, metrics remain inconsistent in their data models and abstraction levels, they exhibit considerable overlaps and are difficult to combine to comprehensively cover a standard's requirement. In this paper, we develop a data model for security metrics based on a systematization of compliance requirements, and we propose a methodology for their elicitation. The method is based on an ontology that enables a systematic development of metrics with a comparable degree of abstraction. We also present our initial work on an open-source effort that demonstrates that our approach also supports a collaborative development of metrics.
tldr: The paper proposes a data model and ontology-driven methodology for systematically eliciting security metrics that make compliance requirements from security standards measurable and automatically checkable.
motivation: Existing security metrics are ad hoc, inconsistent in data models and abstraction levels, overlapping, and hard to combine into full coverage of a standard's requirements, because no systematic elicitation methodology exists.
method: The authors systematize compliance requirements into a data model for security metrics and build an ontology that guides metric development at a comparable abstraction level, alongside an initial open-source collaborative tooling effort.
result: The approach yields systematically derived, comparable metrics that can be combined to cover a standard's requirements, and the open-source effort demonstrates feasibility of collaborative metric development.
conclusion: A structured, ontology-based methodology improves consistency and reusability of security metrics for automated compliance checking, though the work is at an early stage.

title: The Path To Nde 4.0: A Review Of Algorithms, Techniques, And Strategies For Autonomous Inspection
authors: Ashiqur Rahmana, Venkata Devesh Reddy Seethi, Zachary Kral, Austin Yunker, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Hamed Alhoori
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31704v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) is a cornerstone of modern quality assurance, critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of infrastructure and manufactured components without causing damage. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the current NDI landscape, analyzing the field through four distinct lenses, namely, computational algorithms, physical techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives. We synthesize a broad range of academic literature to illustrate the rapid evolution from manual, analog interpretation to a digitized, data-centric paradigm known as NDE 4.0. Our analysis highlights the dominance of ultrasound and visual inspection as primary physical techniques, while revealing a significant shift toward deep learning and generative models for automated defect recognition. Despite these technological strides, the industry faces critical bottlenecks, notably the scarcity of standardized open-access datasets and the "black box" nature of AI models, which hinders widespread adoption. By charting these developments and identifying key research gaps, such as the need for explainable AI (XAI) and standardized digital twin protocols, this review offers a strategic roadmap for future research. It concludes that the future of NDI research should focus on the successful integration of intelligent, autonomous fusion of inspection data with advanced sensor technologies into asset lifecycle management.
tldr: A broad review of non-destructive inspection (NDI) that charts its evolution toward the data-centric 'NDE 4.0' paradigm across algorithms, physical techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives.
motivation: NDI is a cornerstone of quality assurance for infrastructure and manufactured components, and the field is shifting from manual analog interpretation to digitized, AI-driven workflows whose landscape has not been comprehensively mapped.
method: The authors synthesize a wide body of academic literature through four lenses—computational algorithms, physical inspection techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives—to characterize trends and identify gaps.
result: Ultrasound and visual inspection dominate as physical modalities, while deep learning and generative models are increasingly used for automated defect recognition; adoption is limited by scarce standardized open-access datasets and the black-box nature of AI models.
conclusion: The review argues for explainable AI, standardized digital twin protocols, and autonomous fusion of inspection data with advanced sensors integrated into asset lifecycle management as the strategic roadmap for NDI research.

title: Stochastic Geometry Meets Optimization: Data-Driven Cellular Planning
authors: Abhishek K. Shukla, Abhishek K. Gupta, Ketan Rajawat
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deployment optimization of base stations (BSs) is critical for improving cellular network performance metrics such as coverage and capacity, impacting user experience, scalability, and infrastructure cost-effectiveness. Traditional methods that optimize precise BS locations do not generally provide broader insights into spatial deployment priorities or alternative viable deployments. Stochastic geometry approaches, on the other hand, offer a more interpretable intensity-based framework, but rarely utilize real-world user location data or investigate optimal BS deployment strategies. In this work, we propose a data-driven stochastic geometry-based approach that optimizes BS deployment intensity to maximize a network performance metric using samples from an unknown user-location distribution. We specialize the framework to an inhomogeneous Poisson point process (PPP) for cellular coverage analysis. The resulting infinite-dimensional problem is discretized over the deployment area and solved using sampled user locations. We characterize the discretization and sampling errors, apply stochastic mirror ascent to solve the empirical problem, and analyze the selection of concrete BS deployments using independent validation samples. Unlike traditional methods, our approach yields an optimized spatial intensity that reveals deployment priorities across regions and accommodates practical deployment constraints, multi-tier networks, and incremental deployment scenarios. Numerical experiments with synthetic and real-world spatial demand data demonstrate the proposed approach under different network configurations.
tldr: The paper develops a data-driven stochastic-geometry optimization framework for base-station deployment in cellular networks.
motivation: Traditional precise-location optimization gives limited spatial insight, while stochastic geometry is interpretable but often ignores real user-location data and optimal deployment design.
method: It models user locations with an inhomogeneous Poisson point process, discretizes the infinite-dimensional intensity-optimization problem, solves it with stochastic mirror ascent, and analyzes discretization and sampling errors.
result: Numerical experiments on synthetic and real-world spatial demand data show optimized deployment intensities under practical constraints, multi-tier networks, and incremental deployment scenarios.
conclusion: The approach provides interpretable regional deployment priorities and viable base-station placement strategies from sampled user-location data.

title: Mean Estimation In Spatial Functional Data
authors: Qirui Hu Holger Dette
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Functional mean estimation exhibits a sparse-to-dense phase transition as the number of measurements per curve increases. For spatially indexed functional data, however, dependence between nearby curves and increasing spatial sampling density fundamentally alter this transition. We investigate this phenomenon under a unified framework allowing both increasing-domain and infill asymptotics, with irregular temporal observations. Our analysis identifies two distinct sources of estimation error: an observation-level component governed by the total number of measurements and a curve-level component governed by a spatial dependence-adjusted effective sample size. The resulting uniform convergence rates reveal how spatial dependence shifts the temporal phase-transition boundary and how spatial infill can improve estimation through additional measurements without a corresponding increase in effective curve-level information. We establish these results for three spline-based estimators: a pooled estimator of a stationary mean curve, a local-kernel estimator, and a tensor-product estimator of a spatially varying mean surface. The effects of spatial localization on the phase transition are characterized explicitly. Simulations illustrate the interplay between spatial dependence and temporal sampling density, and environmental data applications demonstrate the proposed estimation methods.
tldr: The paper studies mean estimation for spatially indexed functional data, characterizing how spatial dependence and sampling density affect convergence rates and phase transitions.
motivation: Functional mean estimation has a known sparse-to-dense phase transition, but spatially dependent functional data and increasing spatial sampling density require a unified asymptotic framework.
method: The authors analyze three spline-based estimators—pooled, local-kernel, and tensor-product—under increasing-domain and infill asymptotics with irregular temporal observations.
result: They identify observation-level and curve-level error components, derive uniform convergence rates, and show how spatial dependence shifts temporal phase-transition boundaries and how spatial infill can improve estimation.
conclusion: Spatial dependence and infill sampling fundamentally modify functional mean estimation rates and phase transitions, with simulations and environmental data applications illustrating the theory.

title: Incomparable Minima In Agent Tool Authorization
authors: Xin Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent that needs a tool needs authority to call it, and every proposal for governing that authority has to answer one question: of two grants that both let the agent finish a task, which one is smaller? Over-privilege benchmarks score agents against this answer, and permission solvers compute it. We check the question against the authorisation tables that Microsoft and Google publish, covering 22,305 Microsoft Graph endpoint bindings and 23,852 Google API methods, on tasks generated from each table's own resource structure. For 29.8-33.3% of Graph tasks and 3.2% of Google resource tasks the question has no answer, because the minimal sufficient grants form an antichain, a set of grants none of which authorises a subset of what another does. In its two main authorisation modes, Microsoft's shipped privilegeLevel rates 67.4-74.4% of these incomparable pairs equal. Google ships no such scale, so on Google we apply a reconstruction of the FORTIS privilege ladder, which rates 90.7-98.7% equal. Applying the same reconstruction to Graph attributes much of that difference to the scale rather than the corpus: its form based on the HTTP verb alone rates 92.0% of Google pairs and 89.0-92.0% of Graph pairs equal. Four risk measures (operations, writes, services reached, administrative surface) order 28.7% of incomparable Google pairs and 15.7-23.4% of Graph pairs in opposite directions, so for those pairs the ranking has no measure-independent answer. Offered pools of minimal and larger grants, 6 frontier models pick a minimal grant on 99.0% of 1,708 decisions, a grant smallest under all four measures on 66.7%, and on 22.1% a grant that another option matches or beats on every measure. We propose that benchmarks report which minimal grant an agent chose and that deployments show the alternatives to whoever approves the grant.
tldr: An empirical study of whether minimal sufficient tool-authorization grants for LLM agents are uniquely ordered, finding that for a substantial fraction of Microsoft Graph and Google API tasks the minimal grants form incomparable antichains.
motivation: Agent tool authorization requires deciding which of two grants is 'smaller' when both suffice, and over-privilege benchmarks and permission solvers implicitly assume such an ordering exists; the paper tests that assumption at scale.
method: The authors enumerate tasks from the resource structure of 22,305 Microsoft Graph endpoint bindings and 23,852 Google API methods, compute minimal sufficient grant sets, and test for antichains and measure-dependent rankings, then evaluate four risk measures and six frontier models on 1,708 grant-selection decisions.
result: Antichains occur for 29.8–33.3% of Graph tasks and 3.2% of Google resource tasks; Microsoft's privilegeLevel rates 67.4–74.4% of incomparable pairs equal and a FORTIS-ladder reconstruction 90.7–98.7%; four risk measures disagree on 15.7–28.7% of incomparable pairs, and models chose a minimal grant 99.0% of the time but a grant dominated under all measures 22.1% of the time.
conclusion: The authors recommend benchmarks report which minimal grant an agent chose and that deployments surface alternatives to approvers, since no measure-independent minimality ordering generally exists.

title: Non-Expansive Fuzzy Modal Logic Has Uniform Interpolation
authors: Stefan Gebhart, Lutz Schr\"oder, Paul Wild
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fuzzy logics with truth values in the unit interval vary in their choice of propositional connectives and their semantics, ranging from just minimum and maximum as in Zadeh logics to truncated addition and subtraction as in {\L}ukasiewicz logics or their extensions with truth constants, known as Pavelka logics. In the more specific world of fuzzy modal logics, non-expansive fuzzy modal logic has recently been proposed as a sweet spot between {\L}ukasiewicz (more precisely, Pavelka) and Zadeh fuzzy modal logic; it restricts {\L}ukasiewicz propositional connectives to have one argument constant, equivalently extends the Zadeh propositional base with constant shift operators. It retains reasonable expressiveness both in practical terms and abstractly; in particular, it characterizes the standard notion of behavioural distance on fuzzy Kripke frames. At the same time, it allows for satisfiability checking in the same complexity as for its two-valued correspondent (the modal logic K, or the description logic ALC), in contrast to the notorious computational hardness of {\L}ukasiewicz modal logic. In the present work, we show that non-expansive fuzzy modal logic admits uniform interpolation, a key property in modularization, information hiding, summarization, and other applications that fails for both {\L}ukasiewicz (or Pavelka) and Zadeh modal logic.
tldr: The paper proves that non-expansive fuzzy modal logic, a recently proposed intermediate between Łukasiewicz/Pavelka and Zadeh fuzzy modal logics, admits uniform interpolation.
motivation: Uniform interpolation is a key property underlying modularization, information hiding, and summarization of ontologies, and it fails for both Łukasiewicz (Pavelka) and Zadeh fuzzy modal logics; a fuzzy modal logic that retains it while keeping decidability is therefore desirable.
method: The authors work in the framework of non-expansive fuzzy modal logic, whose propositional base restricts Łukasiewicz connectives to one constant argument (equivalently Zadeh connectives plus constant shift operators), and establish uniform interpolation via model-theoretic/algebraic techniques adapted from the two-valued case.
result: Non-expansive fuzzy modal logic is shown to enjoy uniform interpolation, in contrast to both Łukasiewicz/Pavelka and Zadeh fuzzy modal logics where the property fails.
conclusion: The result positions non-expansive fuzzy modal logic as a well-behaved intermediate formalism combining reasonable expressiveness (behavioural distance on fuzzy Kripke frames, K/ALC-level satisfiability complexity) with strong modularity properties.

title: Hybrid Seir Temporal Fusion Transformer Framework With Shap Analysis For Interpretable Pandemic Forecasting
authors: Ashish Anton Abraham, Gopi Krishnan R, Aiswarya Anil Nair, Ajo Babu George, Kunal Agarwal
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forecasting pandemic spread across heterogeneous regions demands models that are both accurate and interpretable for public health action. This paper proposes a hybrid forecasting framework that integrates an SEIR epidemiological model enhanced with a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) to produce interpretable multi-horizon infection forecasts. Using region-wise COVID-19 data from the Our World in Data corpus, we present a unified pipeline that integrates epidemiological indicators (susceptible, exposed, infectious, recovered), intervention signals (masking, vaccination, policies), mobility covariates, and demographic context. The SEIR component estimates latent disease dynamics and injects mechanistic priors, while the TFT learns non-linear temporal dependencies and cross-feature interactions from historical observations and known future inputs. To ensure transparency, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) is applied at both global and local levels, quantifying feature contributions and revealing region-specific drivers of surges and slowdowns. Compared with a calibrated standalone SEIR baseline, the hybrid SEIR-TFT approach provides more stable and accurate forecasts across epidemic phases, particularly under shifting intervention regimes. The framework is further operationalized through structured prediction and explanation outputs for interactive dashboards, enabling time-series, policy-impact, and geospatial analysis. By unifying mechanistic modeling, deep temporal learning, and explainable AI, this study offers a practical decision-support system for policy-sensitive pandemic forecasting.
tldr: A hybrid SEIR-TFT deep learning framework with SHAP explanations for interpretable regional COVID-19 pandemic forecasting.
motivation: Pandemic forecasting across heterogeneous regions requires models that are simultaneously accurate and interpretable enough to guide public health policy decisions.
method: Combines a mechanistic SEIR epidemiological model (supplying latent dynamics and mechanistic priors) with a Temporal Fusion Transformer that learns nonlinear temporal dependencies and cross-feature interactions from mobility, intervention, and demographic covariates, with SHAP used for global and local interpretability.
result: The hybrid SEIR-TFT model yields more stable and accurate multi-horizon forecasts than a calibrated standalone SEIR baseline, especially under shifting intervention regimes, while SHAP identifies region-specific drivers of epidemic surges and slowdowns.
conclusion: The authors present an explainable AI decision-support pipeline with dashboard outputs for policy-sensitive pandemic forecasting; the work is purely epidemiological machine learning with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Anchored Hlld: A Riemann Solver For A Hypoelastic Diffuse-interface Model Of Compressible Fluid-solid Interaction
authors: Tim Colonius Yanjun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an HLLD Riemann solver for a multicomponent hypoelastic diffuse-interface model of compressible fluid-solid interaction, with no separately computed interface and a deviatoric stress advanced by an objective hypoelastic rate law outside conservation-law form. The difficulty specific to this model is that the stress evolution is nonconservative and, unlike the familiar volume-fraction terms of Kapila-type models, cannot be left outside the Riemann solve once the shear waves are resolved. The shear coefficient [MATH] sets the impedance of the resolved shear waves and so belongs to their eigenstructure. Anchored HLLD carries it inside the solve by evaluating the HLLD fan twice at each face, anchored in turn to each adjacent cell-centered state, with every cell advancing from the flux anchored to its own state. HLL, HLLC, and anchored HLLD form a three-tier hierarchy of increasing wave resolution in one framework. We prove local structural properties: consistency at the reconstruction order, exact species-mass conservation, and tangential-momentum and energy drift vanishing under refinement at the reconstruction's face-jump order on smooth fields, with one-dimensional tests illustrating these structural properties and demonstrating first-order drift convergence on discontinuous fields. Across one-dimensional tests and two-dimensional production simulations in the open-source solver MFC, anchored HLLD resolves both the material contact and the shear waves, HLLC the contact alone, and HLL neither sharply. Where refinement studies are shown, anchored HLLD converges toward exact or semi-analytic solutions. A three-dimensional shock-ellipsoid interaction demonstrates the solver with all six stress components active.
tldr: The paper introduces an anchored HLLD Riemann solver for a hypoelastic diffuse-interface model of compressible fluid-solid interaction, resolving shear waves by evaluating the HLLD fan twice per face.
motivation: In hypoelastic diffuse-interface models the deviatoric stress evolution is nonconservative and the shear coefficient belongs to the shear-wave eigenstructure, so stress terms cannot be left outside the Riemann solve as in Kapila-type volume-fraction models.
method: Anchored HLLD evaluates the HLLD fan twice at each face, each anchored to an adjacent cell-centered state, with every cell advancing from the flux anchored to its own state; HLL, HLLC, and anchored HLLD form a three-tier hierarchy of wave resolution.
result: Local structural properties are proved (consistency at reconstruction order, exact species-mass conservation, vanishing tangential-momentum and energy drift under refinement), and 1D/2D tests in the MFC solver show anchored HLLD resolves both material contact and shear waves, converging toward exact solutions.
conclusion: The solver provides a robust, hierarchically extensible framework for compressible multiphase fluid-solid interaction, demonstrated in a three-dimensional shock-ellipsoid interaction with all six stress components active.

title: The Strength Of Root Cuts In An Extended Abstract Branch-and-Cut Model
authors: Aleksandr M. Kazachkov Boyang Han
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The branch-and-cut paradigm has led to effective solvers for a wide range of mathematical optimization problems. Despite significant theoretical work on pure branching and pure cutting, less is known about their interaction. We study an extended abstract branch-and-cut model to investigate tradeoffs between branching and cutting, including the time to generate cuts. We prove that, under symmetric branching, some minimal-time tree has all cuts at the root, before the first branching node, and that there is an asymmetric setting where some minimal-time tree has no internal cuts, i.e., cuts both preceded and followed by branching. For other settings, although a root-cut tree may be suboptimal and differ substantially in structure from a minimal-time tree, it nevertheless provides a reliable approximation whose tree time does not deviate arbitrarily from the optimum. For constant cut strength and bounded time functions, we show that the best root-cut tree is asymptotically optimal as the target bound grows. In addition, under a single-cut-per-path restriction, we characterize when some minimal-time tree has an internal cut. Lastly, simulations indicate that the best root-cut tree is much closer to a minimal-time tree than our worst-case approximation guarantee suggests.
tldr: The paper studies an extended abstract branch-and-cut model to analyze tradeoffs between branching and cut generation in mixed-integer optimization, proving structural properties of root-cut versus minimal-time search trees.
motivation: Although pure branching and pure cutting are well understood theoretically, their interaction in branch-and-cut solvers remains poorly characterized, particularly regarding when cuts should be generated relative to branching.
method: The authors formulate an abstract branch-and-cut model with cut strength and bounded time functions, then prove theorems about the structure of minimal-time trees under symmetric and asymmetric branching, including a single-cut-per-path restriction, supplemented by simulations.
result: Under symmetric branching some minimal-time tree places all cuts at the root; in certain asymmetric settings a minimal-time tree has no internal cuts; for constant cut strength and bounded time functions the best root-cut tree is asymptotically optimal as the target bound grows.
conclusion: Root-cut strategies are provably reliable approximations and often near-optimal in practice, providing theoretical grounding for heuristic cut placement in solvers.

title: Rapid Stabilization For Stokes And Navier-Stokes Systems With Localized Disturbance
authors: Christian Calle, Patricio Guzm\'an, Hugo Parada, Jefferson Prada
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we analyze the rapid stabilization of Stokes and the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems in the presence of an unknown spatially localized disturbance. A multivalued feedback control strategy is proposed which combines the Lyapunov frequency method with the multivalued sign operator. This methodology connects Lyapunov-based stability analysis with spectral inequalities, while the inclusion of the sign operator provides robustness against disturbance. The closed-loop system is governed by a differential inclusion, for which well-posedness is proved via the theory of maximal monotone operators. This approach guarantees global rapid exponential stabilization for the Stokes system and local rapid exponential stabilization for the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems, with arbitrarily large disturbance bounds. In three dimensions, we obtain global strong solutions and rapid exponential stabilization for initial data sufficiently small in the [MATH]-norm with a prescribed, arbitrarily large bound in the [MATH]-norm.
tldr: The paper develops a multivalued feedback control strategy for rapidly exponentially stabilizing Stokes and Navier-Stokes systems subject to unknown spatially localized disturbances.
motivation: Rapid stabilization of fluid flow systems under uncertain, spatially localized perturbations is a challenging control-theoretic problem requiring robustness guarantees.
method: A multivalued feedback law combining the Lyapunov frequency method with a multivalued sign operator is proposed; the closed-loop dynamics form a differential inclusion whose well-posedness is established via maximal monotone operator theory and spectral inequalities.
result: Global rapid exponential stabilization is proved for the Stokes system and local rapid exponential stabilization for 2D and 3D Navier-Stokes systems with arbitrarily large disturbance bounds, including global strong solutions in 3D for sufficiently small initial data.
conclusion: The approach bridges Lyapunov stability analysis with spectral methods and provides robust stabilization guarantees for fluid systems under localized disturbances.

title: Multilevel Monte Carlo For Polytopic Dg Discretisations With Spatially Represented Random Coefficients
authors: Veronika Chronholm, Matt Evans, Emmanuil H. Georgoulis, Tristan Pryer
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a multilevel Monte Carlo framework for coercive elliptic problems with random diffusion and reaction coefficients on polytopic meshes, with particular emphasis on the approximation and inter-level coupling of random coefficients generated from spatially represented latent fields. The main analytical contribution is a Strang-type error decomposition in a DG norm that separates the forward discretisation error from the error introduced by approximating the random coefficients. On this basis, we study two coefficient-generation and multilevel-coupling strategies, a spectral sampler based on a stationary Gaussian latent field defined on a fixed Cartesian reference grid, and an SPDE-based Mat\'ern sampler in which levels are coupled through projected white-noise loads on agglomerated hierarchies. Both fit into the same coefficient-aware analytical framework and couple adjacent levels directly through a common latent random input. The theory is supported by numerical experiments on general Voronoi and agglomerated polytopic meshes, demonstrating the predicted forward and coefficient-representation errors, decay of multilevel corrections, strong inter-level coupling, and the resulting work-accuracy behaviour relative to single-level Monte Carlo.
tldr: A numerical analysis paper developing a multilevel Monte Carlo framework for elliptic PDEs with random coefficients on polytopic discontinuous Galerkin meshes.
motivation: Efficient uncertainty quantification for elliptic problems with spatially varying random diffusion and reaction coefficients requires controlling both discretisation error and the error from representing random fields.
method: The authors derive a Strang-type error decomposition in a DG norm and compare two coefficient-generation/multilevel-coupling strategies: a spectral sampler on a Cartesian latent Gaussian field and an SPDE-based Matérn sampler on agglomerated hierarchies.
result: Numerical experiments on Voronoi and agglomerated polytopic meshes confirm the predicted forward and coefficient-representation error rates, decay of level corrections, and improved work-accuracy scaling over single-level Monte Carlo.
conclusion: The unified coefficient-aware framework enables rigorous error and cost analysis of MLMC for polytopic DG discretisations with random coefficients.

title: Observability From Measurable Sets For Strongly Coupled Parabolic Systems
authors: K\'evin Le Balc'h Xinyi Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize observability of strongly coupled parabolic systems from arbitrary space-time measurable sets of positive measure. For constant coercive diffusion matrices and arbitrary constant zeroth-order coupling and observation matrices, observability holds if and only if the generalized Kalman rank condition is satisfied at every Dirichlet eigenvalue. The diffusion matrix need not be diagonalizable, and the number of components is arbitrary. The observation is measured in [MATH], yielding null controllability with bounded controls by duality. The proof combines a Remez-type inequality for exponential polynomials with a quantitative analysis of the mode-dependent Kalman condition. The resulting finite-dimensional observability estimate is uniform over the spatial modes up to a polynomial frequency loss. A spectral inequality and the Lebeau--Robbiano strategy then give observability of the full system.
tldr: The paper characterizes observability and null controllability for strongly coupled parabolic systems observed from arbitrary measurable space-time sets.
motivation: The work addresses control-theoretic observability for coupled parabolic PDE systems under general diffusion and coupling matrices, extending Kalman-type conditions beyond restrictive diagonal or scalar settings.
method: It combines a Remez-type inequality for exponential polynomials, a quantitative mode-dependent generalized Kalman rank analysis, a spectral inequality, and the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy.
result: Observability holds if and only if the generalized Kalman rank condition is satisfied at every Dirichlet eigenvalue, yielding null controllability with bounded controls by duality.
conclusion: The authors provide a general observability criterion for strongly coupled parabolic systems from measurable observation sets, with uniform finite-dimensional estimates up to polynomial frequency loss.

title: Closed-form Optimal Solutions For Propulsive-Differential Drag Control Of Spacecraft Swarms
authors: Simone D'amico Matthew Hunter
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a novel optimal control approach for Distributed Space Systems (DSS) to minimize the total delta-v cost for large, time-constrained reconfigurations. Reconfiguration cost is decreased by blending differential drag and propulsive control within the same control window. By parameterizing the problem with Relative Orbital Elements (ROE) and leveraging reachable set theory, a maneuver planning methodology is derived to produce provably-optimal, full roto-translational control solutions in closed-form, such that they can be implemented on hardware-limited spacecraft.
tldr: The paper derives closed-form, provably optimal control solutions that blend differential drag with propulsive thrust to minimize delta-v for large, time-constrained reconfigurations of distributed spacecraft swarms.
motivation: Large-scale spacecraft formation reconfigurations under tight time constraints are delta-v expensive, and pure propulsive control is costly while differential drag alone is slow and limited.
method: The problem is parameterized in Relative Orbital Elements (ROE) and analyzed with reachable set theory to synthesize maneuver plans that combine differential drag and propulsion over a shared control window, yielding closed-form full roto-translational solutions implementable on hardware-limited spacecraft.
result: The approach produces provably optimal, closed-form control solutions that reduce total reconfiguration delta-v relative to propulsive-only strategies.
conclusion: Blending differential drag with propulsive control in a single window offers an efficient, computationally tractable route to optimal swarm reconfiguration, suited to resource-constrained spaceborne hardware.

title: A Novel Matrix-Free Approximate Elemental Inverse For Efficient Preconditioning Of Discontinuous Galerkin Spectral Elements
authors: David Moxey Boyang Xia
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient matrix-free preconditioning remains a challenge for discontinuous Galerkin spectral element discretisations of elliptic problems, particularly for general element shapes with collapsed-coordinate bases, such as prisms, tetrahedra and pyramids. Multigrid provides a promising framework, but its efficiency depends strongly on the effectiveness and computational cost of the smoother. For modal bases, point Jacobi can provide insufficient smoothing, whereas applying block Jacobi through stored dense inverses incurs substantial storage and computational costs. We propose a matrix-free approximate elemental inverse, an approximation to the inverse of each elemental diagonal block, constructed from inverse modal-to-nodal transforms and an element-dependent sparse matrix. Its application exploits generalised sum-factorisation and partial sum-factorisation in collapsed coordinates, avoiding the explicit storage and multiplication of large dense matrices. The method is evaluated as both a standalone preconditioner and a multigrid smoother on hexahedral, prismatic, tetrahedral and pyramidal elements. Although the proposed approximation generally increases iteration counts compared to exact block Jacobi, the cost per iteration is far lower. This trade-off yields substantial reductions in total solution time for hexahedral and prismatic elements, while achieving comparable performance for tetrahedral and pyramidal elements. This study can also serve as a practical guide for tuning the convergence of the discontinuous Galerkin interior-penalty Poisson solver.
tldr: The paper introduces a matrix-free approximate elemental inverse, built from inverse modal-to-nodal transforms and sparse element-dependent matrices, to precondition and smooth discontinuous Galerkin spectral element discretisations of elliptic problems on hexahedra, prisms, tetrahedra and pyramids.
motivation: Matrix-free preconditioning for DG spectral element methods on general/collapsed element shapes is difficult: point Jacobi smooths poorly for modal bases, while block Jacobi with stored dense inverses is too memory- and compute-intensive.
method: An approximation to each elemental diagonal block inverse is constructed and applied using generalised and partial sum-factorisation in collapsed coordinates, avoiding explicit storage or multiplication of large dense matrices; it is tested as a standalone preconditioner and as a multigrid smoother.
result: The approximation raises iteration counts relative to exact block Jacobi but greatly lowers per-iteration cost, yielding substantial total time reductions for hexahedral and prismatic elements and comparable performance for tetrahedral and pyramidal elements.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical, storage-efficient smoothing/preconditioning strategy and serves as a tuning guide for DG interior-penalty Poisson solvers.

title: On Exact Critical-Region Boundaries In Continuous-Time Multiparametric Optimal Control Problems
authors: Efstratios N. Pistikopoulos Lida Lamakani
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous-time multiparametric model predictive control solves the optimal control problem once, offline, for every initial state, and divides the initial-state space into critical regions, each with its own control law and sequence of active constraints. A boundary between two regions is either a hyperplane, given by one linear equation, or curved. The curved boundaries have not been computed to date; a classifier has been trained instead to distinguish the regions, so the partition has been known only approximately. In this paper we show that a curved boundary can be computed exactly, without solving any optimal control problem. The method rests on one property. Once the sequence of active constraints is fixed, together with the instants inside it at which a constraint becomes active or inactive (the switching times) and the instant at which the change of the neighboring region first appears (the event time), every condition on a boundary is a linear equation in the initial state, so the computation of a boundary, curved or not, is exact. We fix one of these instants, a switching time or the event time, and solve the linear equations that correspond to it for the corresponding initial state on the boundary; stepping the fixed instant along the horizon yields the whole boundary. A hyperplane is the case in which no instant is left to fix. We illustrate the method on the Newell-Lee evaporator, which has seven critical regions and eight boundaries, four hyperplanes and four curved, computing one boundary of each type in full with the adjacent regions at its ends.
tldr: The paper presents an exact method for computing curved critical-region boundaries in continuous-time multiparametric optimal control problems without solving any optimal control problems.
motivation: In multiparametric model predictive control, the initial-state space is partitioned into critical regions, but curved boundaries between regions could previously only be approximated via trained classifiers.
method: By fixing the sequence of active constraints along with switching times and the event time, all boundary conditions become linear equations in the initial state; stepping a fixed instant along the horizon traces the entire boundary exactly.
result: The approach is demonstrated on the Newell-Lee evaporator with seven critical regions and eight boundaries (four hyperplanes, four curved), computing one boundary of each type together with its adjacent regions.
conclusion: Curved critical-region boundaries in multiparametric optimal control can be computed exactly, removing the need for approximate classifiers in offline control-law synthesis.

title: Piecewise $p_2$ Finite Element Space On Rectangular Meshes In Arbitrary Dimensions For The Biharmonic Equation
authors: Rui Ma, Yang Xing, Shuo Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a piecewise [MATH] finite element space on rectangular meshes in arbitrary dimensions for the biharmonic equation. The discrete space imposes continuity of vertex sums on [MATH]-faces and of averaged normal derivatives across interior [MATH]-faces. A local algebraic characterization of [MATH] is first established through the unisolvence of an enriched polynomial space and the resulting compatibility conditions. For each interior element, a [MATH]-element patch is then introduced, and the associated homogeneous patch space is shown to be one-dimensional. The corresponding patch functions, extended by zero, form a basis of the global homogeneous discrete space. A local quadratic interpolation operator is further constructed in arbitrary dimensions. Its approximation properties, together with a consistency estimate derived from the weak continuity conditions, lead to the optimal broken [MATH] error estimate for the biharmonic problem.
tldr: The paper constructs a piecewise P2 (nonconforming) finite element space on rectangular meshes in arbitrary dimensions for solving the biharmonic equation, with optimal broken H2 error estimates.
motivation: The biharmonic equation requires H2-conforming or nonconforming discretizations; existing low-order element spaces are largely limited to low dimensions or special meshes, motivating a general construction on rectangular meshes in any dimension.
method: The authors establish a local algebraic characterization via unisolvence of an enriched polynomial space, introduce element patches with one-dimensional homogeneous patch spaces yielding global basis functions, and build a local quadratic interpolation operator with consistency estimates from weak continuity conditions.
result: The patch functions extended by zero form a basis of the global homogeneous discrete space, and the interpolation/consistency analysis yields an optimal broken H2 error estimate for the biharmonic problem in arbitrary dimensions.
conclusion: The proposed piecewise P2 space provides a dimension-independent, mathematically rigorous nonconforming finite element framework with optimal convergence for the biharmonic equation.

title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model For Last-Mile Delivery Of Medication In Liberia's Community Health Program
authors: Baris Ata, Yufan Chen, Robert Montgomery
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dynamic allocation of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program. A central warehouse supplies a health facility and the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) it supervises. When a CHA runs out of medication, patients are referred to the facility, incurring travel costs if they complete the referral and remain untreated otherwise. Allocating inventory to CHAs allows more patients to receive treatment without traveling, while retaining inventory centrally preserves flexibility to respond to uncertain demand. The allocation problem must balance these considerations while accounting for fairness across locations. We formulate this problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem whose objective combines the costs of referrals and untreated patients with a demand-weighted fairness utility. Because standard dynamic programming methods are computationally intractable in this setting, we develop a continuous-time approximation that involves controlling the drift rate of a reflected Brownian motion. We then adapt the deep splitting method, using deep neural networks to approximate the value function and its gradient and compute a dynamic allocation policy. We calibrate the model using data on malaria cases among children in the Fangonda region of Lofa County, Liberia, and evaluate the proposed policy in the original discrete-time model. In the baseline setting, our policy reduces operating costs by about 6% relative to the strongest benchmark, the fairness-only policy, while retaining approximately 98% of its fairness utility. Additional experiments show that higher referral costs shift inventory toward CHAs and reduce local unmet demand, while greater demand variability increases our policy's performance over the fairness-only benchmark. Our model and computational approach provide a framework for studying similar last-mile allocation problems.
tldr: The paper develops a stochastic-control and deep-learning-based policy for allocating scarce medications between a central warehouse and community health assistants in Liberia's community health program.
motivation: In last-mile delivery settings, allocating inventory locally to community health assistants reduces patient travel, but retaining stock centrally preserves flexibility under uncertain demand and must also respect fairness across locations.
method: The authors formulate a finite-horizon stochastic control problem combining referral and untreated-patient costs with a demand-weighted fairness utility, then approximate it via controlled drift of a reflected Brownian motion and solve it with a deep splitting method using neural networks to approximate the value function and its gradient.
result: Calibrated on malaria case data from Lofa County, the learned policy reduces operating costs by about 6% versus the strongest fairness-only benchmark while retaining roughly 98% of its fairness utility; higher referral costs shift inventory toward CHAs and greater demand variability improves relative performance.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical computational approach for last-mile medicine allocation and could extend to similar scarce-resource distribution problems.

title: Nadler Theorem On Generalized Metric Spaces With Weighted Graphs
authors: Muhammad Aslam Javed Ismat Beg
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a generalized metric space endowed with a weighted graph and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of fixed points for set-valued mappings that satisfy a contractive condition only along the links of the graph. To demonstrate the applicability and significance of our results, several illustrative examples are presented. As an application, we establish the solvability of a class of integral problems involving set-valued data.
tldr: The paper proves fixed-point theorems for set-valued contractive mappings on generalized metric spaces equipped with a weighted graph, applying the results to integral equations.
motivation: Fixed-point theory on metric-type spaces is a classical tool in nonlinear analysis, and endowing the space with a graph allows contractive conditions to be imposed only along graph links, weakening hypotheses and broadening applicability.
method: The authors introduce a generalized metric space with a weighted graph and derive sufficient conditions for the existence of fixed points of set-valued mappings obeying a graph-contractive condition; illustrative examples and an application to a class of integral inclusions are given.
result: Existence theorems for fixed points of graph-contractive set-valued maps are established, supported by concrete examples and by solvability results for integral problems with set-valued data.
conclusion: The framework extends Nadler-type fixed-point results to graph-weighted generalized metric spaces, offering a flexible analytical tool for nonlinear and integral problems, but it lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: Distributed Attacker Assignment And Interception Control In Multi-Agent Target-Attacker-Defender Games
authors: Pengyang Fan, Shaoqing Zhang, Chao Zhai, Weiguo Xia
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the Target-Attacker-Defender (TAD) game within a planar environment, focusing on the protection of a stationary target against incoming threats. To compensate for potential speed disadvantages of the defenders, we leverage geometric pre-positioning within an annular defense perimeter. The problem is formulated as an area interception problem, for which we propose a distributed multi-agent algorithm consisting of two primary modules: target allocation and interception control. For target allocation, an equitable region partitioning strategy is employed to divide the defense area into annular sectors and assign defenders to attackers. Under specified angular-separation and parameter conditions, the proposed partitioning mechanism ensures that each defender is assigned at most one attacker, thereby reducing the complexity of multi-agent assignment. For the control layer, movement protocols based on zero-sum differential games and coverage optimization are designed, achieving Nash equilibrium strategies while maintaining effective barrier coverage. Numerical simulations show that the proposed method enables slower defenders to intercept faster attackers through proactive deployment and maintains nearly constant local computation time as the swarm size increases.
tldr: The paper develops a distributed two-module algorithm combining equitable annular region partitioning for attacker assignment with zero-sum differential-game and coverage-optimization control protocols, enabling slower defenders to intercept faster attackers in a planar Target-Attacker-Defender game.
motivation: Defenders may be slower than incoming attackers, so the authors aim to compensate by geometrically pre-positioning defenders within an annular defense perimeter and formulating the task as an area interception problem.
method: The defense area is partitioned into annular sectors so that each defender is assigned at most one attacker under angular-separation conditions, and movement protocols are derived from zero-sum differential games and coverage optimization to reach Nash equilibrium with barrier coverage.
result: Numerical simulations show that slower defenders can intercept faster attackers through proactive deployment, while local computation time stays nearly constant as the swarm size grows.
conclusion: Distributed assignment plus differential-game control provides a scalable solution to the TAD interception problem, though the work is purely classical multi-agent control with no quantum information, thermodynamic, or quantum network component.

title: On The Algebraic Structure Of Lewis Carroll's Logic -- Behind The Looking Glass: A Mathematical Perspective
authors: Rainer Picard Sebastian Franz
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charles Ludwidge Dodgeson, better known by his literary pen name `Lewis Carroll', has a number of well known and cherished literary works to his credit, for example "Alice in Wonderland" and "Through the Looking Glass". Apart from this he is known to have a strong professional interest in mathematics and logic with an inclination towards an educational and recreational perspective. In this work we consider the algebraic structure behind Lewis Carroll's approach to classical logic and his logical puzzles. Starting with the arithmetic of [MATH] and [MATH], we develop the connections between Boolean-valued functions, sets and predicates, which we refer to as the "entangled trinity". This provides a common setting in which Carroll's approach and Boole's perspective can be understood. Particular attention is given to what is meant by "the conclusion" of a logical problem. We suggest a precise interpretation of a complete conclusion in terms of largest lower bounds involving only the predicates to be retained, thereby sharpening Carroll's approach. The role of natural language in choosing a suitable universe and identifying these predicates is discussed through a variety of examples. Finally, we present computerised solution methods, including the use of Boolean satisfiability solvers for larger puzzles.
tldr: The paper reconstructs the algebraic structure underlying Lewis Carroll's logical puzzles, unifying his approach with Boole's through Boolean-valued functions, sets, and predicates.
motivation: Carroll's contributions to logic are usually treated as educational or recreational; the authors aim to give them a rigorous algebraic foundation and clarify what constitutes 'the conclusion' of a logical problem.
method: Starting from the arithmetic of Boolean algebras, they relate Boolean-valued functions, sets, and predicates (an 'entangled trinity') to formalize Carroll's and Boole's perspectives, interpret complete conclusions as greatest lower bounds over retained predicates, and implement computerized solvers including SAT-based methods.
result: The framework reproduces and sharpens Carroll's sorites-style reasoning, gives a precise semantics for conclusions via largest lower bounds, and enables automated solution of larger puzzles with Boolean satisfiability solvers.
conclusion: Carroll's logic fits naturally into a Boolean-algebraic setting that bridges his pedagogical style with Boole's formalism, and the resulting formalization supports machine-assisted puzzle solving.

title: A Stochastic Mirror Descent Algorithm For Mean-field Control Problems
authors: Aymen Haouas Noufel Frikha (CES)
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a stochastic mirror descent method for continuous-time McKean-Vlasov control with measure-valued controls and general Bregman regularisation. The dependence on the state law leads to a coupled Wasserstein-Bregman stability problem and to a McKean-Vlasov adjoint equation, which have no counterpart in classical stochastic control. We establish a first-order representation of the cost and prove its relative smoothness in two regimes: nonlinear dynamics with bounded cost derivatives, and affine state-law dynamics with linearly growing cost derivatives, the latter covering linear-quadratic (LQ) and more general nonquadratic models. Our regularity conditions in the control measure are formulated through directional finite increments and do not require second-order flat derivatives. We further introduce relative semiconvexity along admissible forward-backward trajectories, allowing compensation between the dynamics, running cost, and terminal cost beyond pointwise Hamiltonian convexity. This yields energy dissipation, an O(1/n) convergence rate at the convexity threshold, and geometric convergence when regularisation dominates relative nonconvexity. Explicit LQ criteria and numerical experiments illustrate the scope of the results.
tldr: The paper develops a stochastic mirror descent algorithm for continuous-time McKean-Vlasov (mean-field) control problems with measure-valued controls and general Bregman regularization.
motivation: Continuous-time mean-field control with measure-dependent dynamics lacks efficient first-order optimization methods, since the state-law dependence introduces coupled Wasserstein-Bregman stability issues and a McKean-Vlasov adjoint equation absent from classical stochastic control.
method: The authors establish a first-order representation of the cost, prove relative smoothness under two regimes (nonlinear dynamics with bounded cost derivatives; affine state-law dynamics with linearly growing derivatives covering LQ models), and introduce relative semiconvexity along admissible forward-backward trajectories using directional finite increments rather than second-order flat derivatives.
result: They obtain energy dissipation, an O(1/n) convergence rate at the convexity threshold, and geometric convergence when regularization dominates relative nonconvexity, illustrated by explicit linear-quadratic criteria and numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed stochastic mirror descent framework provides a tractable and provably convergent approach to mean-field control, extending first-order methods to measure-valued control settings beyond pointwise Hamiltonian convexity.

title: A Domain-decomposition Reduced-order Model For Two-phase Co$_2$ Sequestration With Moving Wells
authors: Xin He, Xianda Shen, Lei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a domain-decomposition reduced-order model for two-phase geological CO[MATH] storage with fixed and moving wells. The approach builds on a nonoverlapping Schur formulation of a conservative RT0--P0 discretization solved by a sequential pressure--transport algorithm. The distinctive feature of the formulation is that local reduced models are coupled through physically meaningful interface variables: pressure traces for the pressure solve and inflow saturation traces for the transport solve. To address moving wells, we introduce a well-aware strategy that combines source-response enrichment, HAPOD-based far-field compression, and hybrid full-order/reduced-order treatment of well and near-well subdomains. We also formulate conservation-oriented hyper-reduction rules where interface fluxes, boundary terms and source terms are protected. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate accuracy, computational efficiency, robustness of the overall methodology.
tldr: A domain-decomposition reduced-order model is developed for two-phase geological CO2 sequestration simulations with fixed and moving wells.
motivation: Full-order numerical simulation of two-phase CO2 storage with moving wells is computationally expensive, motivating reduced-order surrogates that remain conservative and accurate over long injection horizons.
method: The authors build a nonoverlapping Schur-complement formulation of an RT0-P0 conservative discretization solved by sequential pressure-transport splitting, coupling local reduced models through pressure and inflow-saturation interface traces, and handle moving wells via source-response enrichment, HAPOD far-field compression, and hybrid full/reduced-order treatment of near-well subdomains.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate accuracy, computational speedup, and robustness of the well-aware domain-decomposition reduced-order framework including conservation-oriented hyper-reduction that protects interface fluxes, boundary and source terms.
conclusion: The methodology provides an efficient and conservative reduced-order alternative for subsurface CO2 storage modeling with dynamic well placement.

title: Miace And Monotone Tracking: Exact Tuning For First-Order Plants And Positive Cascades With Pure Delay
authors: Latchezar Tomov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Module of Integral Absolute Complex Error (MIACE) was created by me 23 years ago. It gave very nice behaviour to the transient response of the controlled systems I tested. It combines absolute tracking-error and equilibrium-centered command areas. For a stable unit-gain plant with known pure delay, an exact identity separates squared MIACE excess into a negative-area penalty and a weighted area imbalance. The resulting lower bound depends on the plant's first low-frequency moment and the delay. Every attaining response of a positive cascade is monotone, independently of controller structure. For a first-order plant, output variation and peak overshoot also admit quantitative bounds. Exact conditions identify the unique positive PI controller attaining the delayed bound; filtered PID extends attainment beyond this PI range. For cascades of arbitrary order, Hermite interpolation and a finite-support delay remainder construct proper rational controllers of the same order, with internal exponential stability proved by positive convolution representations. An exponential-moment characterization then closes the attainment question when internal delay blocks are allowed: an ordinary command attains the bound if and only if [MATH]. An explicit internal-model controller realizes every feasible weight and delay. A sharp amplitude-cap condition determines the least command peak among all attaining responses and the complete capped sign-preserving area front. A small-gain estimate supplies an explicit MIACE deviation bound under delay error. A storage balance also extends the exact MIACE identity and monotone attainment to a nonlinear first-order class without delay. Independent physical integrations retain delays exactly; quadratic comparisons provide complementary benchmarks.
tldr: The paper introduces MIACE-based exact tuning and monotone tracking results for first-order plants and positive cascades with pure delay.
motivation: The author aims to characterize exact performance bounds and controller attainment for a tracking-error integral criterion in delayed stable systems.
method: It derives an exact identity splitting squared MIACE excess into area penalties, obtains lower bounds from plant moments and delay, and constructs PI/PID or rational controllers using Hermite interpolation and positive convolution representations.
result: The work provides exact conditions for unique positive PI attainment, proves monotone attaining responses for positive cascades, and gives quantitative bounds on overshoot and command peak.
conclusion: The results provide a sharp control-theoretic characterization of MIACE-optimal tracking under delay, but the paper is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: $L$-tauberian Operators And Subspaces With Equi-integrable Unit Ball
authors: Manuel Gonz\'alez Alberto Caldera
abstract: ArXiv:2610.32432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the class [MATH] of [MATH]-tauberian operators and its dual counterpart, the class [MATH] of [MATH]-cotauberian operators. We obtain sequential, perturbative, and algebraic characterizations of these classes. As a consequence, every [MATH] is disjointly non-singular, and the converse implication holds if and only if every dispersed subspace of [MATH] has equi-integrable unit ball. For [MATH], the latter property depends on [MATH]. For [MATH], equi-integrability of the unit ball is equivalent to dispersedness, and [MATH]-tauberian operators coincide with disjointly non-singular operators, while for [MATH] these equivalences fail. Moreover, [MATH] is neither open nor stable under composition. Applying a result of Haydon, Odell, and Schlumprecht, we show that for [MATH] every infinite dimensional dispersed subspace of [MATH] contains an infinite dimensional subspace with equi-integrable unit ball. However, we give an example showing that this is not true for [MATH].
tldr: The paper introduces L-tauberian and L-cotauberian operators and characterizes them via sequential, perturbative, and algebraic properties in Banach space theory.
motivation: The work aims to extend the theory of tauberian operators by defining L-tauberian classes and relating them to disjointly non-singular operators and equi-integrability of unit balls of dispersed subspaces.
method: The authors develop structural characterizations of L-tauberian and L-cotauberian operators and apply results such as that of Haydon, Odell, and Schlumprecht to study dispersed subspaces for different L.
result: They show that every L-tauberian operator is disjointly non-singular, with the converse depending on equi-integrability properties; these equivalences hold for some L but fail for others, and the class is neither open nor composition-stable.
conclusion: The paper provides a detailed functional-analytic classification of L-tauberian operators and demonstrates sharp differences between parameter regimes, including an example showing a subspace property fails for a particular L.

title: Fooling Llm Safety Guards Into Judging The Wrong Text
authors: Utkarsh Kanwat
abstract: ArXiv:2610.31695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety guards check content before an LLM application acts on it, and most paste that content into a plain-text prompt. Content that imitates the prompt can append a second task, and the guard answers that one instead. We call this target rebinding. Our explanation is that the guard grades the last complete task in its input, here a harmless decoy, so the harmful request goes through unchanged. In a pre-registered test, an appended forged query and decoy clear all 75 held-out AdvBench requests that Shieldstral-1.0-3B flags. The guard is not persuaded: a directive to ignore the text above clears none of them, and in a follow-up run a harmful decoy stops the attack. On our GuardRebind benchmark, each of five guards has an attack family, chosen per guard, that clears at least 93% of its flagged items. Rebinding explains this best on Shieldstral and gpt-oss-safeguard; on ShieldGemma and Llama Guard 3, generic evasion and trailing text respectively do part of the work, and Qwen3Guard falls mainly to a forgery of its whole task. Training the guard to score content no lower than its most harmful part cuts attack success from 75% to 0.8-1.6% on attack families, decoys and forged queries held out of training. All of these attacks append the forged structure after the request, and we added the held-out-decoy evaluation after a first round of test runs. Clean AUROC falls by at most 0.01, but our test of non-inferiority is inconclusive. A score-guided search still beats this trained guard on 47 of 50 items, usually by placing forged structure before the request. On about half of the items where the search wins, the same search also finds benign text, with no forged structure, that clears the guard.
tldr: The paper identifies 'target rebinding', an attack in which adversarial text appended to an LLM safety guard's input causes the guard to evaluate a harmless decoy task instead of the harmful request.
motivation: LLM safety guards often receive pasted plain-text content and may be vulnerable to prompt-injection-style manipulations that redirect their judgment away from the actual harmful content.
